divergences.workedExample:
One cart line: 3 x phone case @ $10, product cost $6 each, no discount, $30 cash tendered.

  Closing PDF:           SUM(10 - 6) over 1 row  =  $4.00
  Dashboard monthly:                                $4.00
  Dashboard chart:                                  $4.00
The closing PDF under-reports this sale's margin by $8.00 (67%). The error scales with quantity: a 10-unit line reports 1/10 of its margin.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp and ProfitRepository are correct. They agree with each other, they carry the quantity factor the schema requires, and the sale value they reconcile against (final_amount_usd = $30) is only consistent with $12 of margin at a $18 cost. The three bare-difference copies are wrong. Not documented as a known gap anywhere: grep for `si.quantity` across docs/ and current_sprint.md returns nothing, and profitRecognition.guard.test.ts never mentions quantity.

The USD half of keep-change diverges too: `kept_change_usd` reaches profit_usd on the stamp (:553) and therefore the Profits page, but the three sale_items-sourced queries can never see it because it is not a sale_item.
divergences.workedExample:
$5.00 sale, product cost $3.00. Customer hands 500,000 LBP; snapshot rate 90,000, so tender = $5.556 and change due is 50,000 LBP. Operator taps "keep change".
  stamp:                  profit_usd $2.00,  profit_lbp 50,000 LBP
  Profits > By User:      $2.00  +  50,000 LBP
  Profits > By Client:    $2.00  +  50,000 LBP
  Profits > By Module:    $2.00  +  "—"        (Profits.tsx:1350-1352 renders 0 as an em dash)
  Profits > By Date:      $2.00  +  0 LBP
  Closing PDF LBP line:   0 LBP  ("Loto only")
  Dashboard net LBP:      0 LBP
Same sale, same day: 50,000 LBP of profit on one tab, "—" on the next.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp plus the By-User/By-Client arms. The money is real — the drawer kept the full 500,000 LBP tender and no OUT leg was written — so the LBP profit exists. ProfitService.ts:548's `profit_lbp: 0` is a literal placeholder, not a computed zero, so it cannot be right; the By-Date omission of `dsp` from the LBP sum is the same omission in SQL form.

divergences.title: A per-item refund never sets sale_items.is_refunded, so every sale_items-sourced surface keeps the refunded line's full margin while the ledger nets it out
divergences.detail: `refundSaleItem` increments only `refunded_quantity` (SalesRepository.ts:1530-1533) and updates `sales.status` to 'refunded' solely when EVERY line is exhausted (:1592-1602). `sale_items.is_refunded = 1` is written in exactly one place in the whole codebase — the whole-sale refund/void path at TransactionRepository.ts:1702. Ledger-sourced readers (ProfitRepository.ts:1303 getSalesProfit, :2330 daily_sales_profit, the By-User/By-Client sale arms) sum SALE + REFUND and net correctly. sale_items-sourced readers gate on `si.is_refunded = 0` (ClosingRepository.ts:874, FinancialRepository.ts:135, SalesRepository.ts:2002, ProfitRepository.ts:1272/:1273) and therefore still count the refunded line in full. `sales.paid_usd` is never reduced by a refund either, so `saleFullyPaid` stays true and the sale keeps passing the closing gate.
divergences.workedExample:
Sale with two qty-1 lines: A = $10 (cost $6), B = $20 (cost $12). Total $30, paid $30 cash. Operator then refunds line A only.
  SALE stamp   +$12.00   ((10-6) + (20-12))
  REFUND stamp  -$4.00   (SalesRepository.ts:1442, no discount)
  ledger net     $8.00   <- the true margin
  Profits > By Module, Profit (USD):  $8.00   (correct)
  Profits > By Module, Revenue (USD): $30.00, Cost (USD): $18.00  (line A still counted)
     -> revenue - cost = $12.00, which contradicts the $8.00 in the profit column on the SAME row
     -> Margin column = 8/30 = 26.7%; the honest figure is 8/20 = 40.0%
  Closing PDF (same day):  $12.00
  Dashboard monthly:       $12.00
  Dashboard chart:         $12.00
$12.00 on the closing document versus $8.00 on the Profits page, for a sale where $10 was handed back.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The ledger (SALE + REFUND) is authoritative — it is the only representation that carries the refund at all, and it is what the generic void/refund machinery is built around (rule 20). The `si.is_refunded = 0` gate is a binary flag being asked to express a partial quantity; `quantity - refunded_quantity` is the value those queries would need. Note this also makes the Profits By-Module row internally inconsistent, since its revenue/cost come from sale_items while its profit comes from the ledger (ProfitService.ts:537-538 mixes the two sources).

  Profits > By Module:  weight 0  ->  $0.00 profit, $0 revenue, count 0 (the sales row is not even emitted, ProfitService.ts:539)

divergences.suspectedAuthority: Profits and Closing. "Profit is real only when money is real" is the stated invariant of packages/core/src/constants/__tests__/profitRecognition.guard.test.ts, and it is exactly the over-recognition class LIRA-160 closed for the other modules (docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md:24). The monthly-tile omission is documented as deliberately deferred; the chart's is not documented at all.

divergences.title: Profits "Revenue (USD)" for sales is the PRE-discount subtotal while every other surface's sale value is the post-discount final, and the Margin % divides by that inflated denominator
divergences.surfaceB: closing (totalSalesUSD) + module table (sale card / detail modal)
divergences.detail: ProfitRepository.ts:1268 sums `si.sold_price_usd * si.quantity`, which is `sales.total_amount_usd` (pre-discount) — the discount lives on the sales row, not on sale_items, and is never joined in. ClosingRepository.ts:825 reports `SUM(final_amount_usd)`. The POS card (ProductSearch.tsx:404) and the detail modal (SaleDetailModal.tsx:529) both show `final_amount_usd`. The Margin column then divides the discount-net profit by the discount-gross revenue: `formatPct(row.profit_usd, row.revenue_usd)` at frontend/src/features/profits/pages/Profits.tsx:1356.
divergences.workedExample:
$100 sale, $20 discount, final $80, product cost $60, paid $80 cash.
  POS sale card / detail modal "Total":     $80.00
  Closing PDF "Total Sales (USD)":          $80.00
  Profits > By Module "Revenue (USD)":     $100.00   <- $20 higher than every other surface
  Profits > By Module "Profit (USD)":       $20.00   (correct)
  Profits > By Module "Margin":  20/100  =   20.0%
  margin on money actually taken: 20/80  =   25.0%
A day of nothing but this sale shows $100 of revenue on the Profits page and $80 on the closing document.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Post-discount final is the authoritative revenue — it is what the customer paid, what the receipt says, what the transaction row stamps as amount_usd (SalesRepository.ts:544-548) and what the closing snapshot reports. The Profits revenue column should subtract the sale-level discount (or the margin denominator should be revenue − discount). Cost is unaffected, so the Profit column stays right; only Revenue and Margin are off.

divergences.title: A partly-settled for-partner sale produces three different margins: proportional on Profits, zero on Closing (accepted), full on the Dashboard (not accepted)
divergences.surfaceB: Dashboard monthly tile + Dashboard chart (full, ungated)
divergences.detail: ProfitRepository.ts:606-611 weights a for-partner sale by `partnerCoverageRatio` (:377-390 — `MAX(0, MIN(1, SUM(covered_amount)/SUM(amount)))` over the sale's FOR_% partner_ledger rows). ClosingRepository.ts:876 uses only `saleFullyPaid`, and a for-partner sale carries paid_usd = 0, so its margin reaches the closing snapshot on no day ever. FinancialRepository.ts:126-141 and SalesRepository.ts:1994-2007 have no gate of any kind, so they book the full margin on the sale's own day.
divergences.workedExample:
For-partner sale, $100 value, product cost $60, partner has so far covered $50 of the $100 FOR_POS ledger row.
  partnerCoverageRatio = 50/100 = 0.5
  Profits > By Module:  profit $40 x 0.5 = $20.00  (revenue $50, cost $30)
  Closing PDF:                             $0.00   (ever — no settlement-day source exists)
  Dashboard monthly tile:                 $40.00   (bare 100 - 60, ungated)
  Dashboard chart:                        $40.00
Three surfaces, three answers, one sale.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Profits ($20) is the intended semantics per the 2026-09-05 proportional-recognition decision. The Closing $0 is a KNOWN, ACCEPTED state — current_sprint.md:3243-3258 records LIRA-173 as CLOSED / WON'T DO with the owner's reasoning (the closing PDF stays a same-day till-cash view; a filed PDF must not change on re-run), and it can only under-count. Do NOT re-file that half. The Dashboard's $40 is the new part: it is over-recognition, undocumented, and is really an instance of divergence 5 (no gate at all) landing on the partner case.

result.notes:
SURFACES 1 AND 2 GENUINELY DO NOT EXIST for this module, and that absence is itself the reason the MTC-class bug cannot occur here in its original form: there is no live profit preview at the POS to disagree with the stamp. It also means the operator has no in-module way to notice any of the seven divergences below — the first place a sales margin appears at all is the Profits page.

ROOT CAUSE OF DIVERGENCES 1, 2 AND 4 IS ONE RULE-14 VIOLATION. "Sales margin" is hand-written in five independent places with no shared fragment:
  packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:522   (item.price - costPrice) * item.quantity        [stamp]      qty YES  discount YES
  packages/core/src/repositories/ProfitRepository.ts:1268 si.sold_price_usd * si.quantity * weight        [profits]    qty YES  discount NO (revenue side)
  packages/core/src/repositories/ProfitRepository.ts:3066 (sold - cost) * si.quantity                     [pending]    qty YES  discount NO
  packages/core/src/repositories/ClosingRepository.ts:871 SUM(si.sold_price_usd - si.cost_price_snapshot_usd)          qty NO   discount NO
  packages/core/src/repositories/FinancialRepository.ts:130 same text                                                  qty NO   discount NO
  packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:1999   same text                                                  qty NO   discount NO
The last three are byte-identical copies of each other. Contrast this with the module's own gate predicates, which ARE properly extracted and shared (saleFullyPaid at ProfitRepository.ts:269, saleRecognitionWeight at :606, notRefunded at :636) — the gates were fixed by LIRA-160/161 and the VALUE expression was not. A single exported `saleMargin(saleAlias, itemAlias)` fragment would close divergences 1, 2 and 4 in one edit.

THE SECOND MTC-CLASS PATTERN (percentage over the wrong currency) IS NOT PRESENT HERE in its LBP form. Sales are USD-priced end-to-end (SalesRepository.ts:544-548 stamps amount_lbp = 0 by design), so `formatPct(row.profit_usd, row.revenue_usd)` at Profits.tsx:1356 always has a real USD denominator for the sales row — it can never show the 0% that the recharge row showed. It is wrong for a different reason (divergence 6: the denominator is pre-discount) and it silently ignores the LBP profit from kept change (divergence 3).

THINGS I CHECKED AND FOUND CLEAN — no divergence:
- Cost basis. The stamp reads `products.cost_price_usd` in a per-item SELECT (SalesRepository.ts:512-521) and `sale_items.cost_price_snapshot_usd` is written by a sub-SELECT of the SAME column in the SAME transaction (:762-765). No update can land between them, so snapshot == stamp basis. product_units has no cost column of its own (electron-app/create_db.sql:311-322), so the LIRA-143 IMEI/warranty work introduced no per-unit cost that could drift from the product-level one.
- Rule 13. SalesService.ts contains no SQL and no profit arithmetic (its only relevant method is a pass-through getChartData at :263). ProfitService assembles repository rows only.
- Refund/stamp symmetry on a WHOLE-sale refund. `_reversePayments` plus the negated stamp plus `is_refunded = 1` (TransactionRepository.ts:1702) net every surface to zero. The divergence is only on the PARTIAL item path.
- Currency conversion. No sales surface converts between USD and LBP, so there is no buy/sell-rate mismatch of the kind flagged for LIRA-174. (The closing PDF converts the AGGREGATE at sell_rate — frontend/src/features/closing/utils/rateStampedProfit.ts — but sales contribute $0 to the LBP side, so that conversion never touches sales money.)

ONE STALE COMMENT WORTH CORRECTING (not a divergence — I verified the code, not the comment). ClosingRepository.ts:1347-1359 states that `salesProfit` "still hand-inlines" saleFullyPaid's formula and lists exporting it as a follow-up. That is no longer true: line 876 calls `${saleFullyPaid("s")}` and the fragment is imported at line 25. The follow-up it describes is already done; the comment will mislead the next reader into "fixing" something that is fixed.

RANKING, if you want one fix first: divergence 1 (missing `* si.quantity`) is the highest-cost item. It is a silent, unbounded under-count on the document the owner files, it is undocumented anywhere in the repo, and it is a three-line change. Divergence 5 (ungated Dashboard arms) is the highest-cost OVER-count — it books profit on money that never arrived, which is the exact invariant profitRecognition.guard.test.ts exists to protect.

surfaces.formula: profit_usd: (data.price_usd ?? 0) - (data.cost_usd ?? 0) + (data.kept_change_usd ?? 0);  profit_lbp: (data.price_lbp ?? 0) - (data.cost_lbp ?? 0) + (data.kept_change_lbp ?? 0). amount_usd/amount_lbp = price_usd/price_lbp. Written for EVERY partner mode — the row is created before the isForPartner / isViaPartner / payments branches at :334+. kept_change_* is accepted by both transports (packages/core/src/validators/customService.ts:25-26 and the desktop duplicate electron-app/schemas/index.ts:803-804), so it really reaches this expression.
surfaces.currencies: transactions.profit_usd and transactions.profit_lbp (both populated independently).

surfaces.location: packages/core/src/repositories/ProfitRepository.ts:1718-1744 (getCustomServicesTotals — feeds ProfitService.getSummary:401 and getByModule:570-582) and :2384-2402 (daily_custom CTE inside getByDate:2218). Also reached generically by getByUser:2750 / getByClient:2910 via PROFIT_TXN_TYPES:954 (ELSE arms at :2844/:2860 and :2997).
surfaces.formula: getCustomServicesTotals: `SUM(t.profit_usd * partnerCoverageRatio('custom_services','cs.id'))` and the same for profit_lbp, revenue from `cs.price_usd/price_lbp * ratio`, cost from `cs.cost_usd/cost_lbp * ratio`, `FROM custom_services cs JOIN transactions t ON t.source_table='custom_services' AND t.source_id=cs.id AND t.type='CUSTOM_SERVICE' WHERE cs.status='completed' AND t.status='ACTIVE' AND notRefunded(cs) AND notDebtPending(t.id) AND dateRange(cs.created_at)`. daily_custom is byte-equivalent, grouped by `DATE(cs.created_at,'localtime')`. getByUser/getByClient instead use `ELSE t.profit_usd * txnPartnerCoverageRatio(t)` with the debt gate, no cs.status gate, and `SUM(t.amount_lbp)` completely ungated for revenue_lbp (:2817, :2973).
surfaces.currencies: profit_usd + profit_lbp, revenue_usd + revenue_lbp, cost_usd + cost_lbp — genuinely per-currency. The Margin column that renders these (frontend/src/features/profits/pages/Profits.tsx:1356) is USD-only.

surfaces.location: packages/core/src/repositories/ClosingRepository.ts:1139-1189 (four schema-degradation branches, `customProfit`), folded into the total at :1333, LBP total at :1360, day predicate `todayLocal` at :56-57
surfaces.formula: `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(profit_usd),0) as profit_usd FROM custom_services WHERE DATE(created_at,'localtime') = DATE('now','localtime') AND status='completed' AND tenant_id=? AND notRefunded('custom_services') AND notPartnerPending('custom_services','custom_services.id') AND notDebtPending(<txn id subquery>)`. Reads the GENERATED source column, never transactions.profit_usd. Folded as `totalProfitUSD = salesProfit + finProfit + rechargeProfit + customProfit.profit_usd + maintProfit + exchangeProfit` (:1329-1335). `totalProfitLBP = lotoProfit.profit_lbp` (:1360) — custom services contribute nothing to it.
surfaces.currencies: USD only. There is no custom-services arm for LBP anywhere in this method.

divergences.title: Kept change is in the transaction stamp but in none of the other four surfaces
divergences.detail: The stamp adds kept change: `profit_usd: (price_usd) - (cost_usd) + (kept_change_usd)` at packages/core/src/repositories/CustomServiceRepository.ts:259-262. Every other surface derives profit from `price - cost` with no kept-change term: the preview at frontend/src/features/custom-services/pages/CustomServices/index.tsx:296-297; the history row and the Today's Profit card via the GENERATED column `profit_usd DECIMAL(10,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (price_usd - cost_usd) STORED` (electron-app/create_db.sql:892, packages/core/src/db/migrations/index.ts:549) read at HistoryModal.tsx:542 and CustomServiceRepository.ts:770; and the closing snapshot, which sums that same generated column at ClosingRepository.ts:1181. Only the Profits page joins `transactions.profit_usd` (ProfitRepository.ts:1726). This is the exact MTC/SMS shape: one concept, four independent definitions of it, one of which grew an extra term. kept_change_usd/lbp is fully wired on both transports (packages/core/src/validators/customService.ts:25-26; electron-app/schemas/index.ts:803-804) and is set by MultiPaymentInput's onKeptChange (index.tsx:1202, packages/ui/src/components/ui/MultiPaymentInput.tsx:1134), so this is live, not theoretical.
divergences.workedExample:
Service 'Screen protector install', cost $3.00, price $5.00. Customer hands $6.00 cash and the operator ticks 'Keep change' ($1.00 kept).
  preview (index.tsx:296)          5.00 - 3.00              = $2.00
  history row / Today's Profit     GENERATED (5.00 - 3.00)  = $2.00
  closing snapshot (:1181)         SUM(profit_usd)          = $2.00
  transaction stamp (:259-262)     5.00 - 3.00 + 1.00       = $3.00
  Profits > By Module (:1726)      SUM(t.profit_usd)        = $3.00
Same sale, $2.00 on the Services page and in the closing PDF, $3.00 on the Profits page.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp is correct. Kept change is real profit the shop physically holds (it is the drawer excess the customer walked away from — MultiPaymentInput.tsx:1116-1131 computes it from the actual tender), and T3 KC-3 deliberately routed it into profit. The generated column cannot see it because kept change is not a column on custom_services, so the fix is to stop deriving profit from `price - cost` in three more places and read transactions.profit_usd everywhere (the closing arm especially — it already has the transaction id to hand at :1139-1142).

divergences.title: An LBP-denominated custom service contributes zero profit to the daily closing snapshot, in either currency
divergences.detail: The closing arm selects only `SUM(profit_usd)` (ClosingRepository.ts:1150, 1160, 1171, 1182) and is added only into `totalProfitUSD` (:1333). There is no `SUM(profit_lbp)` counterpart anywhere in the method for custom services, and `totalProfitLBP = lotoProfit.profit_lbp` (:1360) — loto only. The Profits page, the stamp, the preview and the history row all carry profit_lbp as a first-class figure (ProfitRepository.ts:1727; CustomServiceRepository.ts:263-266; index.tsx:297; HistoryModal.tsx:542). The gap is documented as a known state at frontend/src/features/closing/utils/rateStampedProfit.ts:31-48, which states plainly that a genuine LBP profit slice 'is dropped from BOTH totals today, not merely deferred'. The Services page is single-currency-per-entry by design (index.tsx:144, the USD/LBP toggle clears the other currency's fields), so an LBP service is an ordinary case, not an edge one.
divergences.workedExample:
Service 'SIM activation', cost 200,000 LBP, price 300,000 LBP, cash paid, no partner.
  preview (index.tsx:297)             300,000 - 200,000  = 100,000 LBP
  history row (generated profit_lbp)                     = 100,000 LBP
  stamp (CustomServiceRepository:263)                    = profit_lbp 100,000, profit_usd 0
  Profits > By Module Profit (LBP)                       = 100,000 LBP
  closing totalProfitUSD  (:1333)     SUM(profit_usd)    = $0.00
  closing totalProfitLBP  (:1360)     lotoProfit only    = 0 LBP
A day whose only trade is this service prints a daily closing profit of $0.00 / 0 LBP while the Profits page for the same day shows 100,000 LBP.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The Profits page is correct. The closing snapshot needs a `SUM(profit_lbp)` arm for custom services folded into totalProfitLBP, exactly as LIRA-161 did for loto. Note LIRA-174 (docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md §3) is about to print a rate-converted USD total from totalProfitUSD+totalProfitLBP — it will convert a number that is silently missing every LBP custom service, so this gap gets multiplied rather than exposed.

divergences.title: Partner coverage on a for-partner service is gated three different ways: not at all, proportionally, and all-or-nothing
divergences.detail: A FOR-mode service books the full price as a `FOR_CUSTOM_SERVICE` partner_ledger DEBIT (CustomServiceRepository.ts:370-394) and still stamps the full price-cost margin at :259-266. Three consumers then disagree about when that margin is earned: (a) getTodaySummary (CustomServiceRepository.ts:761-778) applies no partner gate at all and recognises it immediately; (b) getCustomServicesTotals scales every column by `partnerCoverageRatio('custom_services','cs.id')` (ProfitRepository.ts:1722-1728, defined :377-390) — a continuous `SUM(covered_amount)/SUM(amount)` fraction; (c) the closing arm applies `notPartnerPending('custom_services','custom_services.id')` (ClosingRepository.ts:1184, defined ProfitRepository.ts:289-297) — a binary NOT EXISTS that excludes the whole row until the LAST cent is covered. (b) and (c) are two hand-maintained encodings of one rule (rule 14): the ratio fragment's own doc at :371-376 says it was added as the proportional replacement, and the closing call site was never converted.
divergences.workedExample:
For-partner service, cost $60, price $100 → stamped profit $40. The partner later settles $50 of the $100 ledger row (covered_amount = 50, amount = 100).
  Services page 'Today's Profit' (getTodaySummary, no gate)     = $40.00
  Profits > By Module  (ratio 50/100 = 0.5 x $40)               = $20.00
  Closing snapshot     (50 < 100 - 0.005 -> row excluded)       = $0.00
Three surfaces, three numbers, for one service on one day.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The proportional form (Profits) is the current owner decision — ProfitRepository.ts:1712-1716 records it as 'Owner decision 2026-09-05: a for-partner job recognises proportionally to partner coverage across every monetary column'. The closing arm is stale (it was wired binary by LIRA-160 on 2026-09-04, one day before that decision), and getTodaySummary has no gate at all, which is the most wrong of the three: it books partner money as today's profit before any of it has arrived.

divergences.title: The module's own Today's Profit card keeps counting voided and refunded services
divergences.detail: getTodaySummary (packages/core/src/repositories/CustomServiceRepository.ts:761-778) has neither a `status` filter nor `notRefunded`. Its sibling read path one method up, getAll at :646, does filter `WHERE status != 'voided'`, and every other surface gates both ways: the closing arm has `status='completed' AND notRefunded('custom_services')` (ClosingRepository.ts:1183) and the Profits arm has `cs.status='completed' AND notRefunded(cs)` (ProfitRepository.ts:1731-1733). Void sets `custom_services.status = 'voided'` (CustomServiceRepository.ts:738-741); refund sets `is_refunded = 1` via TransactionRepository._markSourceRefunded (:1644). The card is therefore the only surface in the module that recognises money for a transaction whose cash was already given back — a rule 20 reversal gap on the read side.
divergences.workedExample:
Service cost $4.00, price $10.00 → generated profit $6.00. The operator voids it the same day from the Transactions viewer.
  Services page 'Today's Profit' (:770-773, no gates)  = $6.00
  Services page History list     (:646, status filter) = row not listed at all
  Profits > By Module            (:1731)               = $0.00
  Closing snapshot               (:1183)               = $0.00
The card claims $6.00 of profit from a service that its own history table refuses to show. Refund (rather than void) gives the same $6.00 on the card, against a struck-through row and $0.00 on both reports.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: getTodaySummary is wrong; the other three agree with each other. The one-line fix is the same predicate pair already used two files away: `AND status = 'completed' AND ${notRefunded('custom_services')}`.

divergences.title: Today's Profit compares a UTC date against a local date, so services entered after local midnight vanish from the card
divergences.detail: getTodaySummary's predicate is `DATE(created_at) = DATE('now','localtime')` (CustomServiceRepository.ts:773) — the left side has no `'localtime'` modifier, so it is the UTC calendar date, while the right side is the local one. `created_at` is written as `COALESCE(?, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)` (:148), and SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is UTC; the backdating override also sends UTC (`date.toISOString()`, frontend/src/shared/components/TransactionTimeOverride.tsx:53, typed by `transactionTimeSchema` = `z.string().datetime()`, packages/core/src/validators/common.ts:38). The two surfaces that agree with each other both convert the column: ClosingRepository's `todayLocal` is `DATE(col,'localtime') = DATE('now','localtime')` (:56-57), and ProfitRepository's `dateRange` is `datetime(col,'localtime') >= ? AND <= ?` (:664-666) bound to local day edges. This is a third hand-written day predicate for one concept (rule 14).
divergences.workedExample:
Beirut is UTC+3. A service (cost $3, price $5) is entered at 01:30 on 2026-09-06 local; created_at is stored as '2026-09-05 22:30:00'.
  getTodaySummary:  DATE('2026-09-05 22:30:00') = '2026-09-05'  vs  DATE('now','localtime') = '2026-09-06'  -> no match -> Today's Profit $0.00
  closing todayLocal: DATE('2026-09-05 22:30:00','localtime') = '2026-09-06' = today -> included, $2.00
  Profits dateRange:  datetime(...,'localtime') = '2026-09-06 01:30' is inside [2026-09-06 00:00:00, 23:59:59] -> included, $2.00
And it never appears on 2026-09-05's card either, because by the time the row exists the local date is already the 6th — so the sale is permanently invisible on the module's own dashboard while both reports carry it.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The closing/Profits form is correct (LOCAL_BUSINESS_DAY_PLAN.md is the established convention, cited in ProfitRepository.ts:653-662). getTodaySummary should use the same `todayLocal` fragment rather than a fourth copy. Caveat worth carrying: docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md §4 trap 5 records that under core jest on Windows SQLite's `'localtime'` resolves to +1 while JS resolves to +3, so a test written for this will read differently locally than on CI — that is a test-harness artefact (LIRA-168), not a reason to doubt the production behaviour.

divergences.title: A loss-making custom service renders as "$0.00" on all three module surfaces and as a real negative on the Profits page
divergences.detail: The module's formatter drops any component that is not strictly positive: `if (usd > 0) parts.push(...); if (lbp > 0) parts.push(...); return parts.join(' + ') || '$0.00'` — three independent copies of the same helper, at frontend/src/features/custom-services/pages/CustomServices/index.tsx:70-75, HistoryModal.tsx:100-105, and StatsCards.tsx:17-22. A negative profit therefore falls through to the literal '$0.00'. The surrounding code knows the value is negative and only recolours it red (index.tsx:966-972, HistoryModal.tsx:528-536, StatsCards.tsx:44-48), so the sign is conveyed by colour and the magnitude is destroyed. The Profits page uses the currency-context formatter, which is unconditional (frontend/src/contexts/CurrencyContext.tsx:128-144) and prints the negative. Cost > price is a legitimate entry — the form explicitly accepts cost-only submissions (index.tsx:301-308) and the validator only requires one of the four amounts to be non-zero (packages/core/src/validators/customService.ts:82-91).
divergences.workedExample:
Service where the shop ate a loss: cost $10.00, price $4.00 → profit -$6.00.
  preview  (index.tsx:974)         formatCurrency(-6, 0)   -> 'Profit: $0.00' (in red)
  history row (HistoryModal:542)   formatCurrency(-6, 0)   -> '$0.00' (in red)
  Today's Profit (StatsCards:51)   formatCurrency(-6, 0)   -> '$0.00' (in red)
  stamp (CustomServiceRepository:259)                      -> profit_usd = -6.00
  Profits > By Module (Profits.tsx:1332)                   -> '$-6.00'
The operator entering the loss is told it is zero. LIRA-153 fixed precisely this class of bug on the Profits page's LBP column (Profits.tsx:1338-1345 comment: 'a LOSS must be visible'); the same fix was never carried into the Services module's own three formatters.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The Profits page is correct. The `> 0` guards were written to suppress an empty currency in a dual-currency string, and they silently swallow negatives as a side effect. The guards should be `!== 0` (matching what LIRA-153 did for row.profit_lbp), or all three copies should be replaced by the shared currency formatter.

divergences.title: The Profits Margin column divides USD profit by USD revenue, so every LBP custom service shows 0%
divergences.detail: frontend/src/features/profits/pages/Profits.tsx:1356 renders `formatPct(row.profit_usd, row.revenue_usd)` for every module row, including the CUSTOM_SERVICE row assembled at packages/core/src/services/ProfitService.ts:570-582. formatPct (:291-294) returns the string '0%' whenever the total is 0. The row itself carries revenue_lbp and profit_lbp, which the two adjacent columns render (:1325-1350), so the data for a correct per-currency margin is right there in the same object. This is the second defect the MTC row exposed, reproduced identically for this module.
divergences.workedExample:
Same LBP service as above: price 300,000 LBP, cost 200,000 LBP, no USD component.
  row.revenue_lbp = 300,000   row.profit_lbp = 100,000   row.revenue_usd = 0   row.profit_usd = 0
  Margin cell: formatPct(0, 0) -> total === 0 -> '0%'
  True margin: 100,000 / 300,000 = 33.3%
The row shows 'Revenue (LBP) 300,000 / Profit (LBP) 100,000 / Margin 0%' on one line.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The Profit (LBP) column is right and the Margin cell is wrong. Margin needs to be per-currency (two cells, or one cell computed from whichever currency the row actually has revenue in). Note this is not custom-services-specific — the same cell computes the margin for every module row, so any LBP-native module (loto, LBP recharges, mobile services) reads 0% too.

divergences.title: The Dashboard's monthly P&L omits custom-service profit entirely
divergences.surfaceA: dashboard monthly P&L (a sixth surface, outside the five)
divergences.detail: FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL (packages/core/src/repositories/FinancialRepository.ts:114-196) is composed of exactly three terms: sale-item margin (:126-140), service commissions from the two financial-service arms (:145-153), and expenses (:159-175). `netProfitUSD = salesResult.profit + commissionUsd - expenses` (:175-176) and `netProfitLBP = commissionLbp - expenses` (:178). There is no custom-services term — nor maintenance, recharge, loto or exchange. The Dashboard consumes it as the headline monthly figure (frontend/src/features/dashboard/pages/Dashboard.tsx:388, 396-397). ProfitService.getSummary over the same month does include custom services in both gross_profit_usd and gross_profit_lbp (packages/core/src/services/ProfitService.ts:475, 486).
divergences.workedExample:
A month whose only trades are 10 custom services at cost $3 / price $5 each ($20 total margin), plus $0 sales, $0 commissions, $0 expenses.
  Profits page, gross/net profit (ProfitService.ts:475)  = $20.00
  Dashboard monthly net profit (FinancialRepository:175) = 0 + 0 - 0 = $0.00
The Dashboard reports a zero-profit month that the Profits page reports as $20.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The Profits page is the complete figure; the Dashboard tile is a partial one presented as 'net profit'. Whether to widen getMonthlyPL or relabel the tile is an owner call — LIRA-159 (docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md §1) already reworked this method once for commission correctness without adding the missing modules, so the omission looks deliberate-by-inertia rather than decided. Flagging because it is the same class of silent per-module disappearance as the closing gap above, not because I can prove intent.

divergences.title: Profits By-User/By-Client LBP revenue is completely ungated while By-Module's is partner- and debt-gated
divergences.detail: getByUser and getByClient compute `SUM(t.amount_lbp) AS revenue_lbp` as a bare aggregate with no CASE at all (packages/core/src/repositories/ProfitRepository.ts:2817 and :2973), while the USD sibling one line above is wrapped in the full CASE carrying `WHEN NOT notDebtPending(t.id) THEN 0` and `* txnPartnerCoverageRatio(t)`. The By-Module arm scales LBP revenue by the coverage ratio (:1723). Profit is not affected (both LBP profit arms are gated at :2860/:3013), and refunds still net out because the REFUND row stamps negated amounts (TransactionRepository.ts:1620-1626) — the exposure is confined to revenue_lbp on deferred rows. This is the live instance of the LIRA-169 note in docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md §3 ('profitRecognition.guard.test.ts is defeatable by a gated sibling column (live in getByUser/getByClient)').
divergences.workedExample:
One for-partner LBP custom service, price 300,000 LBP, cost 200,000 LBP, partner has settled nothing (covered_amount = 0).
  Profits > By Module, Revenue (LBP):  300,000 x ratio 0.0 = 0 LBP
  Profits > By User,   Revenue (LBP):  SUM(t.amount_lbp)   = 300,000 LBP
Same page, two tabs, same single transaction, 300,000 LBP apart. (Profit agrees at 0 in both tabs.)
divergences.suspectedAuthority: By-Module is right — deferred partner money is not revenue yet. revenue_lbp in both generic methods should carry the same CASE its USD sibling already has. Lower blast radius than the others above since only revenue, not profit, is affected.

result.notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Every cite below was opened and read; I did not trust any comment about code over the code itself, and I re-checked the two claims the whole report leans on. (1) `custom_services.profit_usd` really is a generated column on BOTH schema paths — `electron-app/create_db.sql:892-893` for a fresh DB and `packages/core/src/db/migrations/index.ts:549-550` for a migrated one. This mattered: if the migrated path had a plain column, the INSERT at CustomServiceRepository.ts:144-171 (which does not list profit_usd) would leave it 0 and the finding would have been a far larger bug instead of a drift. It is generated on both. (2) kept change genuinely reaches the repository on both transports — `kept_change_usd/lbp` are present in the core validator (validators/customService.ts:25-26) AND in the hand-duplicated desktop schema (electron-app/schemas/index.ts:803-804, which is explicitly labelled a rule-14 local duplicate). Had it been missing from the desktop copy, Zod would strip it and divergence 1 would be web-only.

ROOT CAUSE, STATED ONCE. `profit = price - cost` for this module exists in four independent, hand-maintained definitions: the SQL generated column (create_db.sql:892-893), the JS stamp expression (CustomServiceRepository.ts:259-266), the React preview (index.tsx:296-297), and — implicitly — the closing arm's choice to sum the generated column rather than the stamp (ClosingRepository.ts:1181). Divergence 1 is what happens when one of four copies grows a term. Divergences 2, 3, 4 and 5 are the same shape applied to the *gates* around that number (currency split, partner coverage, refund/void, business day) rather than the number itself. There is no single named definition of "custom-service profit" anywhere in the codebase to point a fix at; ProfitRepository's `notRefunded` / `notDebtPending` / `notPartnerPending` / `dateRange` fragments show the pattern the module should have followed.

WHAT I DID NOT FIND. The VIA-partner mode is clean: it books a `THROUGH_CUSTOM_SERVICE` partner_ledger CREDIT (CustomServiceRepository.ts:589-612) whose transaction_type does not match the `FOR\_%` pattern used by both partnerCoverageRatio (:381) and notPartnerPending (:293), so it correctly recognises immediately on every surface and stamps price-cost like a walk-in. The debt gate is consistent — `notDebtPending` is applied identically in the Profits arm (:1732) and the closing arm (:1183) and is keyed on the same `Custom Service Debt` charge type (:412). The exchange_rate stamped on the row does not enter any profit formula (every surface is per-currency, nothing converts), so the MTC-class "one surface uses a different rate" defect does not exist here. Refunds net correctly in the generic per-user/per-client arms because the REFUND row negates the stamp.

TWO SMALLER THINGS THAT DID NOT EARN A DIVERGENCE ENTRY (no worked example with two user-visible numbers). (a) `exchange_rate` is sent by the form (index.tsx:376-380) but is absent from the desktop IPC schema `CustomServiceCreateSchema` (electron-app/schemas/index.ts:775-820) while present in the core/web one (validators/customService.ts:46) — so on desktop Zod strips it and the repository falls back to the live snapshot rate. It changes the rate stamped on the transaction row for display, not any profit figure, so no two surfaces disagree on money. (b) getByUser/getByClient have no `cs.status = 'completed'` gate, so a `status: 'pending'` custom service would contribute profit there but not in By-Module or the closing snapshot. The current UI never sends `status` (the payload at index.tsx:370-415 omits it, so the schema default 'completed' applies), so it is unreachable from the app today — a latent drift, not an observable one.

SURFACES I COULD NOT LOCATE: none. All five exist for this module. The "table" surface has two distinct halves (per-row history modal and the Today's-* cards) reading the same generated column through different queries; I recorded both under the one entry because they share the formula and disagree with each other only via the gates already reported in divergences 4 and 5.

UNRELATED ENVIRONMENT NOTE: this session reported that the claude.ai Gmail and Sentry MCP connectors need authorization and cannot be authorized from a non-interactive session. Neither was needed for this audit.

result.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — I could not refute this. Every cited line is exact, the schema premise is proven, and the divergent branch is trivially reachable by an ordinary operator.

SCHEMA PREMISE (the load-bearing input): `sold_price_usd` and `cost_price_snapshot_usd` are UNIT values. Both — and only two — INSERT paths prove it. `electron-app/create_db.sql:369-371` declares `quantity INTEGER`, `sold_price_usd DECIMAL(10,2)`, `cost_price_snapshot_usd DECIMAL(10,2)` as three separate columns. `packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:763-767` binds `item.quantity` into `quantity` and `item.price` into `sold_price_usd`, with `cost_price_snapshot_usd` taken as a scalar sub-select of `products.cost_price_usd` — a per-unit catalogue cost, never multiplied. `SalesRepository.ts:901-909` is the matching `.run()`. The second insert path, `addSaleItem` at `SalesRepository.ts:1303-1306`, is identical in shape. There is no third writer (`grep "INSERT INTO sale_items"` over core/backend/electron-app returns only these two).

THE THREE BARE-DIFFERENCE QUERIES — all three lines exact:
- `packages/core/src/repositories/ClosingRepository.ts:871` `COALESCE(SUM(si.sold_price_usd - si.cost_price_snapshot_usd), 0) as profit_usd`, inside `getDailyStatsSnapshot()` (`ClosingRepository.ts:814`).
- `packages/core/src/repositories/FinancialRepository.ts:130` `COALESCE(SUM(si.sold_price_usd - si.cost_price_snapshot_usd), 0) as profit`, inside `getMonthlyPL` (`FinancialRepository.ts:114`).

result.correction:
The finding stands. Two refinements to the write-up, neither of which weakens it:

1. NARROW THE "CLAIMED AUTHORITY". "The stamp and ProfitRepository are correct, they agree with each other" is true only for the worked example's shape — an undiscounted, fully-paid, non-partner sale. In general the stamp and `getSalesRevCost` do NOT agree: the stamp subtracts the sale-level discount (`SalesRepository.ts:530`) and adds kept change (`:553`), while `ProfitRepository.getSalesRevCost` (`:1264-1277`) applies `saleRecognitionWeight("s")` and no discount at all. Citing their mutual agreement as the authority is fragile. The durable authority is the schema plus a same-file witness: `create_db.sql:369-371` stores unit price, unit cost and quantity in three separate columns, and `SalesRepository.ts:1872` already writes `SUM(si.sold_price_usd * si.quantity)` for `total_revenue` — so the identical file multiplies for revenue and forgets to for profit at `:1999`. Any sum of these two columns that omits `* si.quantity` is wrong under every reading, independent of which reporting surface one trusts.

2. TIGHTEN THE SCHEMA CITE. `SalesRepository.ts:901-911` is the `.run()` call; the decisive evidence is the INSERT column list and its scalar cost sub-select at `SalesRepository.ts:763-767`, plus the second writer `addSaleItem` at `SalesRepository.ts:1303-1306` (which the write-up does not mention and which behaves identically — worth naming so a fix does not assume a single insert path).

Also worth adding to the ticket, since it bears on blast radius: the Dashboard tile (`FinancialRepository.ts:126-138`) and the Dashboard chart (`SalesRepository.ts:1996-2007`) carry no fully-paid gate, so the under-report is unconditional there, whereas the Closing PDF arm (`ClosingRepository.ts:868-878`) additionally requires `saleFullyPaid("s")` — the shortfall only reaches the PDF for sales that are fully settled. And per rule 14, the fix should not be three independent edits: the three sites should call one shared named margin fragment rather than each growing its own `* si.quantity`.

divergences.surfaceB: profits + closing + the Dashboard monthly P&L
divergences.detail: ExpenseRepository.getTodayExpenses (packages/core/src/repositories/ExpenseRepository.ts:221) hand-writes `status != 'voided'` and carries NO is_refunded gate. The four reporting queries all use the shared activeExpense() fragment (packages/core/src/repositories/ProfitRepository.ts:642-644), which is `status = 'active' AND COALESCE(is_refunded,0) = 0` — BOTH columns. This matters because an expense can be undone through two doors that flip DIFFERENT columns, exactly as activeExpense's own doc comment (:624-641) states: ExpenseRepository.deleteExpense (:241-256) sets status='voided' AND voids the transaction (both columns flip, everyone agrees); but a void driven from the Transactions viewer runs TransactionRepository.voidTransaction, whose step 4 calls _markSourceRefunded (TransactionRepository.ts:1398 → :1917-1945), which UPDATEs `is_refunded = 1, refunded_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` on `expenses` (whitelisted at :1929) and NEVER touches `status`. So that row reads status='active', is_refunded=1 — excluded by activeExpense(), included by `status != 'voided'`. The drawer leg has already been given back by _reversePayments. This is the exact hole ExpenseActiveGate.test.ts was written for (packages/core/src/repositories/__tests__/ExpenseActiveGate.test.ts:1-28); that ticket fixed ClosingRepository and FinancialRepository and left getTodayExpenses, the one surface the operator actually looks at while working, ungated. divergences.title: The Expenses page's "today" is the UTC day; every reporting surface's "today" is the local day — a 3-hour nightly blind spot in Beirut
divergences.surfaceA: table (ExpenseRepository.getTodayExpenses, which feeds BOTH the header totals and the entire History modal)
divergences.detail: ExpenseRepository.ts:221 is `DATE(expense_date) = DATE('now')` — bare, no 'localtime' modifier on either side, so both sides are UTC. ClosingRepository.ts:56-57 is `DATE(col,'localtime') = DATE('now','localtime')`, and ProfitRepository.ts:666-668's dateRange is `datetime(col,'localtime') >= ? AND datetime(col,'localtime') <= ?` against JS-computed local-day bounds. The written value makes the gap concrete: Expenses/index.tsx:123 sends `expense_date: new Date(formData.expense_date).toISOString()` where formData.expense_date is localDay() (a LOCAL 'YYYY-MM-DD'), and a date-only string parses as UTC midnight — so a manual expense is stored as local-day-at-00:00Z. The renderer's own localDay doc (frontend/src/shared/utils/localDay.ts:3-10) warns about exactly this rollover and the page then reintroduces it one line below. I verified the SQLite arithmetic directly (python stdlib sqlite3 3.50.4, machine at UTC+3): DATE('2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z') = '2026-09-05'; datetime('2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z','localtime') = '2026-09-05 03:00:00'. Caveat: docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md §4 item 5 (LIRA-168) records that under core jest on Windows SQL 'localtime' resolves to +1 while JS resolves to +3 — that changes the width of the window, not its existence, since the two predicates are textually different in any timezone east of UTC.
divergences.workedExample:
Beirut, UTC+3. It is 01:30 local on Fri 2026-09-05 — i.e. 22:30 UTC on Thu 2026-09-04. Operator books a 500,000 LBP Bill expense.

  Expenses page reload (ExpenseRepository.ts:221): DATE('2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z') = '2026-09-05'; DATE('now') = '2026-09-04' (still Thursday in UTC). '2026-09-05' != '2026-09-04' → row NOT returned. Header reads Total LBP: 0. The expense the operator just typed is gone from the screen, and the History modal is empty.
  Closing snapshot (ClosingRepository.ts:861): DATE(expense_date,'localtime') = '2026-09-05'; DATE('now','localtime') = '2026-09-05' → match. Total Expenses (LBP): 500,000.
  Profits for 2026-09-05 (getExpenseTotals): datetime(expense_date,'localtime') = '2026-09-05 03:00:00', inside ['2026-09-05 00:00:00','2026-09-05 23:59:59'] → counted, 500,000 LBP deducted.

0 vs 500,000 vs 500,000, for three hours every night.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The reporting surfaces are correct — the whole app moved to the local business day (docs/plans/done_plans/LOCAL_BUSINESS_DAY_PLAN.md, cited at ClosingRepository.ts:54-55) and getTodayExpenses is the straggler. divergences.title: Two writers encode expense_date differently — Line_Usage stores a real UTC instant, manual expenses store local-midnight-as-UTC
divergences.surfaceB: stamp, LIRA-145 Line_Usage path (CarrierLineRepository.ts:907 → the same createExpense)
divergences.detail: One column, two encodings. Expenses/index.tsx:123 writes `new Date(formData.expense_date).toISOString()` — a local 'YYYY-MM-DD' re-parsed as UTC midnight, so the stored instant is 00:00Z of the LOCAL day. CarrierLineRepository.ts:907 writes `new Date().toISOString()` — the true UTC instant of the click. Downstream, three consumers slice or truncate this column differently: ExpenseRepository.ts:221 takes the UTC day, ClosingRepository.ts:861 and ProfitRepository.ts:1882/:2440 take the local day, and the History modal's filter (useDateRangeFilter via HistoryModal.tsx:40-43, frontend/src/shared/hooks/useDateRangeFilter.ts:17) takes `String(item.expense_date).slice(0,10)` — a raw string cut, which is the UTC day for a Line_Usage row and the local day for a manual row. divergences.workedExample:
Beirut, UTC+3. 01:30 local on Fri 2026-09-05 (22:30 UTC Thu 2026-09-04). Two expenses booked one minute apart:
  (a) Manual $20 Shop_Supply → expense_date = '2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z'.
  (b) Record-usage on an MTC line, $8 → expense_date = '2026-09-04T22:30:00.000Z'.

  Same page at 10:00 local the SAME business day (UTC day now = 2026-09-05): (a) → SHOWN. (b) DATE = '2026-09-04' → now HIDDEN. Header Total USD: $20.00.

$8.00, then $20.00, versus $28.00 — for the same two expenses, on the same day.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Line_Usage's `new Date().toISOString()` is the more honest value (it is the real moment) and is what a 'localtime' reader wants; the manual path's local-midnight-as-UTC only survives because the readers below it happen to use 'localtime'. But the divergence is not resolvable at the write side alone — the reads must agree first. Fix the read side per the previous entry, then normalise both writers to the same encoding. Do not change the writers alone: repointing the manual path would silently shift historical rows across day boundaries in the closing snapshot.

Second-order asymmetry inside the PDF itself: the profit block converts LBP→USD at sell_rate (LIRA-174), the expense lines are not converted at all, so an operator cannot even do the subtraction in one currency without redoing the rate math by hand.
divergences.workedExample:
One day: $80.00 USD gross profit across sales/services, 90,000 LBP loto commission, and expenses of $50.00 USD + 1,000,000 LBP. Sell rate 90,000.

  Closing PDF (closingReportGenerator.ts:138-141):
    Total Expenses (USD): 50.00
    Total Expenses (LBP): 1,000,000
    Profit - USD amount: $80.00
    Profit - LBP amount (Loto only): 90,000 LBP
    Profit - Total (USD) @ 90,000 (sell rate): $81.00      <- 80 + 90,000/90,000
    Profit - Total (LBP) @ 90,000 (sell rate): 7,290,000 LBP
  Profits page, same day: Net Profit (USD) = 80.00 - 50.00 = $30.00; Net Profit (LBP) = 90,000 - 1,000,000 = -910,000 LBP.

The operator reads "Profit - Total (USD): $81.00" off the closing PDF and "$30.00" off the Profits page for the same day, and a POSITIVE 7,290,000 LBP against a NEGATIVE 910,000 LBP.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Neither number is arithmetically wrong — this is a labelling/semantics divergence, and it is the lowest-severity item here because the PDF does print the expense lines two rows above. But the label "Profit - Total" reads as the day's bottom line and is not. Cheapest honest fix: rename to "Gross Profit - Total" and add a "Net of expenses" line using the SAME sell_rate conversion the block already stamps. Do NOT silently start deducting expenses inside totalProfitUSD without the owner: LIRA-174's recorded decision (docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md §3) was about the conversion rate, not about gross-vs-net, so the question has not actually been put to them.

divergences.title: Split-payment mode makes the form's "Total Amount" show only the first line while the submitted expense is the sum of all lines
divergences.surfaceA: preview (MultiPaymentInput "Total Amount" row, fed by the Expenses page's self-referential totals prop)
divergences.detail: This is the structural twin of the MTC case: the preview and the write are two independent expressions over the same concept. Expenses/index.tsx:251-258 hands the widget its OWN first payment line as the target — totals={[{amount: paymentLines[0]?.amount || 0, currency: paymentLines[0]?.currencyCode || "USD"}]}. Inside the widget baseTotals = totalsProp (MultiPaymentInput.tsx:385), totalInTarget = sumInTarget(baseTotals) (:419), and the rendered "Total Amount" row is that value (:1743-1747) — i.e. line[0].amount, always, no matter how many lines exist. The submit handler does something different: index.tsx:112-115 iterates EVERY line (`paymentLines.forEach(line => { if (line.currencyCode === "USD") amount_usd += line.amount; if (line.currencyCode === "LBP") amount_lbp += line.amount; })`) and sends the sum. The page's own comment at :102-103 says "Use the first payment line (single-mode only)" and the code four lines below contradicts it. Split mode is reachable — the toggle at MultiPaymentInput.tsx:1342-1345 (data-testid="split-toggle") renders unconditionally, and the auto-sync that would keep line[0] equal to the total is explicitly skipped in split mode (:459-460, :500). The widget's own "Paid" row (:812-815, :1832+) does sum all lines and will show a red mismatch marker, but it is comparing against a target that is itself one of the lines being summed, so the marker reads as "you overpaid", not as "the total is wrong".
divergences.workedExample:
Operator records a supplier run paid partly in each currency: line 1 = $40.00 CASH, then hits Split and adds line 2 = 900,000 LBP CASH. Rate in the widget = buyRate, say 89,000.

  Widget "Total Amount" (MultiPaymentInput.tsx:1743-1747): totalInTarget = sumInTarget([{40, USD}]) = $40.00. Displayed: $40.00.
  Widget "Paid" (:812-815): 40 + 900,000/89,000 = 40 + 10.11 = $50.11, with a red cross (|50.11 - 40| = 10.11 > 0.01).
  Submitted (index.tsx:112-115, :118-125): amount_usd = 40, amount_lbp = 900,000.
  Transaction stamp (ExpenseRepository.ts:129-130): amount_usd = -40, amount_lbp = -900,000. Two drawer legs, -$40 USD and -900,000 LBP (:200-206).
  Closing PDF that evening: Total Expenses (USD) 40.00, Total Expenses (LBP) 900,000 — i.e. about $50.11 of value, against the $40.00 the form said the expense was.

The operator's confirmation screen said $40.00; the books took $40.00 + 900,000 LBP.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp is right — both legs really did leave a drawer, and both must be recorded. The preview is wrong, and the root cause is the self-referential totals prop: a payment widget's total must be an INDEPENDENT amount the operator states, not a mirror of one of its own lines. Two defensible fixes: (a) give the page a real amount field and feed that as totals, so "Total Amount" and the Paid check both mean something; or (b) if expenses are genuinely single-line by design, pass a prop that hides the split toggle and drop the all-lines loop at :112-115 in favour of firstLine only. Do NOT just change the submit handler to read line[0]: that would silently discard a leg the operator entered, and the drawer posting at ExpenseRepository.ts:200-206 would then move money the expense row does not record.

divergences.title: getTodayExpenses hand-writes the status half of activeExpense() instead of calling the fragment (rule 14 drift, equal today)
divergences.detail: Distinct axis from the is_refunded finding above: even the STATUS half is a second, hand-written copy. `status != 'voided'` and `status = 'active'` are equivalent only because electron-app/create_db.sql:600 declares `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'` and the only other value any writer ever sets is 'voided' (ExpenseRepository.ts:250-254 is the sole UPDATE of the column in production code). They also happen to agree on NULL by accident — SQL's `NULL != 'voided'` is NULL (falsy) and `NULL = 'active'` is false, so a NULL-status row is excluded by both, but for different reasons. The moment anyone adds a third status ('pending_approval', 'archived', 'draft' — any of which is a plausible next feature) the two definitions split, silently, in opposite directions: the deny-list keeps the new status, the allow-list drops it. This is precisely the rule-14 case: the predicate is already defined once as an exported fragment and is not being called.
divergences.workedExample:
Hypothetical but one migration away. Suppose a 'pending_approval' status is added for expenses over $500, and a $600 expense sits in it awaiting the owner's sign-off (no drawer leg posted yet, or posted and awaiting review).

  Expenses page, `status != 'voided'`: 'pending_approval' != 'voided' → TRUE → row included. Header Total USD: $600.00.
  Closing PDF and Profits, `status = 'active'`: 'pending_approval' = 'active' → FALSE → row excluded. Total Expenses: $0.00.

$600.00 vs $0.00, from a schema change that touched neither query. Today, with only 'active'/'voided' ever written, both return the same set — so this costs nothing yet and is listed as a drift risk, not a live bug.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: activeExpense() is authoritative — it is the documented single definition (ProfitRepository.ts:624-644) and already governs four of the five production reads of the table. Folding getTodayExpenses into it is the same one-line edit that fixes the is_refunded divergence, so both should land together. GOOD NEWS worth recording alongside: after that one line, ALL five production `FROM expenses` queries (ExpenseRepository.ts:220, ClosingRepository.ts:860, FinancialRepository.ts:166, ProfitRepository.ts:1881 and :2443) share one predicate text with zero copies.

result.notes:
WHAT AGREES — stated plainly, because it is most of the module. The four reporting reads of the `expenses` table are in genuine, textual agreement and I found no arithmetic difference between them: ProfitRepository.getExpenseTotals (:1873-1886), ProfitRepository's daily_expenses CTE (:2438-2447), ClosingRepository.expensesStats (:855-865) and FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL's expenses block (:160-174) all call the SAME activeExpense() fragment, all bound the date on datetime/DATE(expense_date,'localtime'), all sum amount_usd and amount_lbp as independent per-currency figures, and all net them per-currency with no conversion (ProfitService.ts:515-516, ProfitRepository.ts:2485-2486, FinancialRepository.ts:186-188). There is no cost the expense arm subtracts that another does not, and no rate applied on one side and not the other. The MTC archetype's exact shape — a hand-rolled preview formula competing with a repository formula for the same profit concept — does not occur here for profit, because expenses carry no profit: the stamp writes profit_usd = profit_lbp = 0 (TransactionRepository.ts:515-516) and no surface reads it. Every divergence above is in the module's own page or in a presentation layer, not between the money queries.

A SIXTH SURFACE, outside the five you named: the Dashboard's monthly net-profit tile. FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL (:160-188) → Dashboard.tsx:388, :396-397, :855-856. It is gated identically to the Profits page and I found no divergence in it, but it is a second net-profit-after-expenses figure on a different screen and belongs on any map of this module.

MODULE-PAGE DEFECTS THAT ARE NOT TWO-SURFACE DIVERGENCES, so I did not file them above:
1. HistoryModal.tsx:203 renders the literal string "Cash" in the "Paid By" column for every row. paid_by_method IS projected (ExpenseRepository.ts:95) and IS on the interface (HistoryModal.tsx:13). A Line_Usage expense (paid_by_method 'LINE_CREDIT', which moved a carrier credit drawer, not cash — CarrierLineRepository.ts:906, ExpenseRepository.ts:174-182) and a BINANCE expense (which moved USDT, ExpenseRepository.ts:192-197) both display as "Cash". Same class as the LIRA-119/121/122/129/131 family the sprint board calls out at current_sprint.md:729-733: money correct, screen wrong.
2. The History modal can only ever show today. It is passed `expenses` (Expenses/index.tsx:311), which is getTodayExpenses' output, and its DateRangeFilter is a client-side filter over that array (HistoryModal.tsx:40-43 → useDateRangeFilter.ts:14-22) — from/to can only narrow, never widen. A figure on the Profits or Closing surface for any prior day cannot be reconciled against the module's own history at all. There is no getExpensesByDateRange method on the repository.
3. Its export buttons are labelled exportFilename="expenses-history" (HistoryModal.tsx:156) and export the same today-only rows.

THE ARCHETYPE'S SECOND CLASS (margin from the wrong currency) — present on the Profits page but NOT on an expenses row. Profits.tsx:1356 computes the By-Module Margin column as formatPct(row.profit_usd, row.revenue_usd) (helper at :291), USD columns only, on a table whose rows include LBP-native modules. LOTO is the clean case: ProfitService.ts:619-630 pushes revenue_usd: 0 and profit_usd: 0 with all the money in the LBP fields, so a loto row showing 450,000 LBP profit on 5,000,000 LBP revenue renders Margin from 0/0 — exactly the 0%-on-a-real-margin symptom in your brief. I am reporting it only as context: expenses have no By-Module row at all (see the getByModule finding), so this specific cell can never be an expenses cell. It belongs to whoever audits loto / mobile services.

VERIFICATION METHOD AND CAVEATS. Every line cite above was read from the file in this session, not from a comment about the file; where a comment and the code disagreed I followed the code (e.g. PostRefactorVerification.test.ts:1499's title says getTodayExpenses "uses DATE(created_at)" — it uses expense_date). The SQLite date arithmetic in divergences 2 and 3 I executed rather than reasoned about, using Python's stdlib sqlite3 (3.50.4, zero ABI coupling per the handover's trap 6 — no build, no rebuild, nothing that could disturb desktop e2e): DATE('2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z') = '2026-09-05' and datetime('2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z','localtime') = '2026-09-05 03:00:00' on this UTC+3 machine. One caveat carried forward: LIRA-168 (handover §4 item 5) records that under core jest on Windows, SQL 'localtime' resolves to +1 while JS resolves to +3 — that would change the WIDTH of divergence 2's nightly window in a test fixture, not its existence, since the two predicates differ textually in any non-UTC zone. I ran no tests, builds, yarn, npm or Playwright, and changed no file.

I located all five surfaces; none was missing. The one partial absence is surface 4: ProfitService.getByModule (ProfitService.ts:528-679) has no expenses arm, so the Profits "By Module" tab omits the module even though the Summary and By-Date tabs both deduct it — filed as its own consequence inside the By-Date finding rather than as a separate divergence, because nothing there displays a WRONG number, a row is simply absent.

RANKING, if you are filing tickets: divergence 1 (is_refunded gap) first — it is live today, needs one line, and ExpenseActiveGate.test.ts already holds the two-door fixture to extend for rule 17. Then divergence 6 (split-mode preview), which is the true MTC-class defect here and the only one that can make the operator confirm one amount and book another. Then 4 (LBP vanishing from the Daily tab). Divergences 2, 3 and 7 travel together with 1 in the same file. Divergence 5 needs an owner decision before any code moves.

result.correction:
The claim stands as written. Three refinements for the ticket body, none of which weaken it:

1. SCOPE NARROWING (blast radius). SalesRepository.ts:829-855 rejects `item.quantity !== 1` on any line carrying a `product_unit_id`, and current_sprint.md:2057-2058 records the rule: "Unit-tracked cart lines are quantity-1 (one unit per line; selling 3 phones = 3 lines)." So IMEI/unit-registered goods — phones — cannot trigger this. The divergence is confined to non-unit-tracked products sold with quantity > 1: accessories, cases, chargers, SIMs. The claimant's phone-case example is exactly right, but the ticket should say the defect cannot affect unit-tracked inventory.

2. A SECOND DIVERGENCE IN THE SAME THREE QUERIES, unmentioned. The stamp also subtracts the sale-level discount at SalesRepository.ts:530 `saleProfitUsd -= sale.discount || 0` (rationale at :492-495: the discount comes out of margin). None of ClosingRepository.ts:871, FinancialRepository.ts:130, or SalesRepository.ts:1999 subtracts it. So even a quantity-1 discounted sale diverges from the stamp — these three over-report by the full discount there, while under-reporting on multi-unit lines. A fix that only adds `* si.quantity` leaves the discount half open. (ProfitRepository handles the discount separately via `saleRecognitionWeight` at :1268/:2311 — verify that arm before copying it.)

3. AUTHORITY IS STRONGER THAN STATED. The claimant listed the stamp plus five ProfitRepository lines. Add three more quantity-carrying sites: SalesRepository.ts:1872 (`SUM(si.sold_price_usd * si.quantity)` as total_revenue), SalesRepository.ts:1399 and :1413 (refund math multiplies by refundQuantity), and packages/core/src/db/migrations/index.ts:2918. That is eight quantity-carrying sites against three bare ones — the three are unambiguously the outliers.

4. NAMING PRECISION. "Closing PDF" is the checkpoint report PDF (Checkpoint/index.tsx:301-341), and since LIRA-174 the figure prints inside a rate-stamped combined USD+LBP profit block (closingReportGenerator.ts:113-122,141), not a standalone "Total Profit" line — relevant to whoever writes the guarding assertion.

5. RULE 14 NOTE for the fix: this is the exact shape rule 14 forbids — one business predicate copied into eight places. The correct fix extracts a single named SQL fragment (alongside the existing `saleFullyPaid`/`saleRecognitionWeight`/`notRefunded` fragments already used in these files) rather than patching `* si.quantity` into three more copies. Per rule 17, prove each of the three with a failing-first test on a quantity-3 line.
