divergences.workedExample:
Rates LBP: buy 89,000 / market 89,500 / sell 90,000. Two economically equivalent $100 trades on the same day, nothing else booked.

(a) Customer sells 9,000,000 LBP for USD (LBP->USD, sell_rate leg): amount_out = 9,000,000/90,000 = $100.00. profit = computeLegProfitUsd(9,000,000, LBP, fromIsUsd=false) = 9,000,000 x 500 / 89,500^2 = $0.5618.
(b) Customer buys LBP with $100 (USD->LBP, buy_rate leg): amount_out = 100 x 89,000 = 8,900,000 LBP. profit = 100 x 500 / 89,500 = $0.5587.

Profits > By Module > Currency Exchange, per row:
  (a) Revenue (USD) $9,000,000.00 | Profit (USD) $0.56 | Margin (0.5618/9,000,000)x100 = 0.0000062% -> prints "0.0%" | cost_usd $8,999,999.44
  (b) Revenue (USD)       $100.00 | Profit (USD) $0.56 | Margin (0.5587/100)x100 = 0.559% -> prints "0.6%" | cost_usd $99.44
Combined row: Revenue $9,000,100.00, Profit $1.12, Margin 0.0%. The Total Revenue tile reads $9,000,100 for two hundred-dollar trades.
History modal for the same two rows: "9,000,000 LBP -> 100 USD" and "100 USD -> 8,900,000 LBP" — correct, and irreconcilable with the $9,000,100.
This is the same shape as the MTC 0%-margin symptom: a percentage whose denominator is in the wrong currency.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The history table is right; the Profits query is wrong. `amount_in` is unambiguously native-currency (ExchangeRepository.ts:298, :414, and the schema comment at electron-app/create_db.sql:644 sits directly under `from_currency`). The fix belongs in ProfitRepository.getExchangeTotals / daily_exchange: convert to USD per row (the row already stores leg1_rate/leg1_market_rate/via_currency, so a per-row USD notional is derivable without a live rate lookup), or drop `revenue_usd` for exchange entirely and let Margin fall back to the profit-only presentation. Note the ordering asymmetry is the proof it is not a deliberate "notional turnover" choice: the same trade contributes 100 or 9,000,000 purely by direction.

divergences.title: For-partner exchange profit is recognised three different ways: proportional in Profits, all-or-nothing in Closing, gross in the History modal
divergences.detail: ProfitRepository.getExchangeTotals (:1851) and daily_exchange (:2453) weight the leg-profit sum by `partnerCoverageRatio` (ProfitRepository.ts:377-390: `COALESCE((SELECT MAX(0.0, MIN(1.0, SUM(covered_amount)/NULLIF(SUM(amount),0))) FROM partner_ledger WHERE reference_table='exchange_transactions' AND reference_id=... AND transaction_type LIKE 'FOR\_%'), 1.0)`) — a continuous fraction. ClosingRepository.ts:1321 gates the SAME rows with `notPartnerPending` (ProfitRepository.ts:289-296: `NOT EXISTS (... AND covered_amount < amount - 0.005)`) — a binary include/exclude. HistoryModal.tsx:387-390 applies neither. Partial coverage is genuinely reachable: PartnerRepository.applySettlementCoverage (:424-469) allocates a settlement FIFO across open FOR_% rows and writes a partial `covered_amount`. The exchange's FOR_EXCHANGE row is booked at `amount = Math.abs(data.amountIn)` in fromCurrency (ExchangeRepository.ts:576-593). The comment at ClosingRepository.ts:1298-1301 still asserts the closing arm is "matching getExchangeTotals's own gate set exactly" — that stopped being true when getExchangeTotals switched to the proportional weighting (owner decision dated 2026-09-05 in its own docstring at :1843-1846), so the stale comment is itself the tell.
divergences.workedExample:
A for-partner exchange booked today: partner stands in for the customer, from LBP 9,000,000 -> shop disburses $100. leg1_profit_usd = $0.5618, leg2_profit_usd = NULL. partner_ledger FOR_EXCHANGE row: amount = 9,000,000 LBP. Partner settles half today: covered_amount = 4,500,000.

  ratio = MAX(0, MIN(1, 4,500,000 / 9,000,000)) = 0.5

  Profits (getExchangeTotals):  0.5618 x 0.5            = $0.28   (and revenue_usd 9,000,000 x 0.5 = 4,500,000)
  Closing (notPartnerPending):  4,500,000 < 9,000,000-0.005 -> EXISTS -> row excluded = $0.00
  History modal:                (0.5618 ?? 0) + (NULL ?? 0)                             = $0.56

Three surfaces, three numbers, one transaction, same day. At 0% coverage they read $0.00 / $0.00 / $0.56; at 100% they read $0.56 / $0.56 / $0.56. The disagreement window is exactly the partial-settlement window.
Second-order: because the closing snapshot is dated by exchange.created_at only, a partner who settles on a later day never restores that profit to ANY closing PDF (there is no settlement-day arm for exchange, unlike financial-service commission) — the same gap-of-omission class already ticketed as LIRA-173 for sales, but for exchange it is undocumented.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Profits is the newer and more deliberate definition (the 2026-09-05 proportional decision, docstring at ProfitRepository.ts:1843-1846). Closing has not been migrated and its own comment still claims parity it no longer has. History being gross is defensible as a per-transaction record rather than a recognition surface, but it shares the column name "Profit" with the two surfaces that gate — at minimum it should carry the same [partner]/pending marker the transactions table uses. Recommend: point the closing arm at partnerCoverageRatio (or export a single shared exchange-profit fragment used by both) and correct ClosingRepository.ts:1298-1301.

divergences.title: The live preview zeroes the acquire leg on a cross exotic->exotic trade where the server keeps that leg's full profit
divergences.detail: frontend/src/features/exchange/pages/Exchange/index.tsx:580 zeroes leg 1 on `fromIsLotTracked` ALONE — `isLotTrackedCurrency(fromCurrency)`, i.e. any non-USD/non-LBP currency (packages/core/src/constants/exchangeLotPolicy.ts:38-40). The server does not: `_applyExchangeLotEffects` needs a USD anchor for a cross, and when `_crossUsdNotional` (ExchangeRepository.ts:834-857) finds neither side is LBP and neither side has an `exchange_rates` row it returns null, and the hook bails at ExchangeRepository.ts:705-708 with `touched:false`, leaving `leg1_profit_usd` at the client-sent value. The preview's own consume-leg branch DOES handle this case (index.tsx:582-584 falls back to leg.profitUsd when `lotPreview.lotTracked` is false, which ExchangeLotService.previewSettlement returns with `reason: "NO_RATE_ANCHOR"`, ExchangeLotService.ts:180-190) — and the UI comment at index.tsx:1271-1275 states the intent outright: "the profit figures above already fall back to the plain spread model, which is what the server will actually keep." That fallback was applied to line 581 and not to line 580. Reachability: exotic->exotic pairs are selectable because `effectiveRates` merges live-feed rates for any selected currency missing from the DB (index.tsx:429-437, useExchangeCurrencyList.ts:104-125), and feed currencies get buy_rate == sell_rate == market_rate (liveExchangeRates.ts:151-175) so they never appear in `exchange_rates`. With no rate override both legs are 0 either way; the divergence needs the operator to type a leg rate — which is the normal way these trades are priced.
divergences.workedExample:
Pair GBP -> AED. Neither has an `exchange_rates` row (both feed-only). amountIn = 1,000 GBP. Feed GBP: market_rate 1.30 USD/GBP, is_stronger -1, buy == sell == 1.30. Feed AED: market 3.67 AED/USD, is_stronger +1, buy == sell == 3.67. Operator overrides leg 1 to 1.20 USD/GBP (he buys the GBP under market).

  leg1 (GBP->USD), applyCustomRates (index.tsx:474-508):
     actualOut = 1000 x 1.20 = 1,200 USD ; marketOut = 1000 x 1.30 = 1,300 USD
     computeOverrideLegProfitUsd(1300, 1200, null)  = (1300 - 1200) x 1 = +$100.00
  leg2 (USD->AED), untouched, feed spread = 0:
     computeLegProfitUsd(1200, AED) = (1200 / 3.67) x (0/2) = $0.00

  PREVIEW header (index.tsx:1164-1165, via displayLegProfits :580-586):
     leg1 -> 0 (fromIsLotTracked)
     leg2 -> lotPreview.lotTracked === false (NO_RATE_ANCHOR) -> leg.profitUsd = 0
     Total +$0.0000

  SUBMIT (index.tsx:946-951) sends leg1ProfitUsd = 100, leg2ProfitUsd = 0, totalProfitUsd = 100.
  SERVER: _crossUsdNotional -> not LBP, no rate row for GBP, none for AED -> null -> touched:false
     exchange_transactions.leg1_profit_usd = 100.00, profit_usd = 100.00; transactions.profit_usd = 100.00

  Profits, Closing and the History modal all then report $100.00 for a trade the operator was shown as $0.0000.

The mirror case also exists and is the more dangerous direction: with the override the OTHER way (operator overpays, leg1 = -$100.00), the preview still shows $0.0000 while the books take a $100 loss.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The server is authoritative and correct — `touched:false` is the deliberate "skip lot tracking, keep the spread model" path (documented at ExchangeRepository.ts:695-702). The preview is wrong. Fix at index.tsx:580: gate the acquire-leg zeroing on the same signal the consume leg already uses, i.e. only zero leg 1 when the pair actually has an anchor (the preview call already learns this — `lotPreview.reason === "NO_RATE_ANCHOR"`), or call `crossPairHasUsdAnchor` (packages/core/src/utils/lotMarketRate.ts:75-79) directly, which exists precisely to keep these two decisions in lockstep.

divergences.title: The FIFO preview and the FIFO stamp divide by different denominators — raw leg amount vs the rounded amount actually submitted
divergences.detail: frontend/src/features/exchange/pages/Exchange/index.tsx:830 computes `unitProceedsUsd = usdIn / rawQty` where `rawQty = consumingLeg.amountOut` (:822, the UNROUNDED calculator output), while the quantity actually sent to the preview is the rounded one (`previewQty = parseFloat(amountOut)`, :842 — `amountOut` is the state string set by `totalAmountOut.toFixed(getDecimals(toCurrency))` at :661 and :686). The server never sees the raw value: ExchangeRepository.ts:751-754 computes `unitProceedsUsd = data.amountIn / data.amountOut` from the ROUNDED submitted amount. So the two FIFO runs use the same qty but a different per-unit price. The in-file comment at index.tsx:816-819 explicitly chose to keep the raw denominator ("the guard and the FIFO cost-basis ratio still use the raw, unrounded leg amount") while switching only the qty — that is exactly what makes the two definitions disagree. Same class on the cross path, where the preview uses `consumingLeg.amountIn` and the server uses `_crossUsdNotional / data.amountOut`.
divergences.workedExample:
USD -> EUR, direct. EUR rates buy 1.16 / market 1.18 / sell 1.20 (is_stronger -1, from the local exchange_rates table so the pair IS anchored). amountIn = $1,000. One open lot at unit_cost_usd 1.16 with more than enough qty.

  raw amountOut = 1000 / 1.20 = 833.333333...   submitted amountOut = "833.33" (2dp)

  PREVIEW (index.tsx:830 -> ExchangeLotService.previewSettlement -> previewConsume):
     unitProceedsUsd = 1000 / 833.333333... = 1.20000000
     profit = round2(833.33 x (1.20000000 - 1.16)) = round2(33.33320) = $33.33
     UI prints "Realized profit: $33.3300 USD" (index.tsx:1347-1356)

  STAMP (ExchangeRepository.ts:753 -> consumeFifo -> ExchangeLotRepository.ts:452):
     unitProceedsUsd = 1000 / 833.33 = 1.20000480
     profit = round2(833.33 x (1.20000480 - 1.16)) = round2(33.33720) = $33.34

  leg1_profit_usd = 33.34 is what Profits, Closing and the History modal all report; the operator was shown 33.33.
The gap scales with how much rounding the toFixed() drops, so it is cents on ordinary tickets and grows with a 0-decimal target currency.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The server is authoritative (it prices against the money that actually moves, the rounded amount_out). The preview should divide by `previewQty`, not `rawQty` — one line at index.tsx:830 — so that both sides consume the identical (unitProceedsUsd, qty) pair. Note the cost-basis rule itself is clean: consumeFifo and previewConsume share ONE walker (ExchangeLotRepository.ts:384-537), so this is purely the inputs disagreeing, not the algorithm.

divergences.title: EXCHANGE_LEG_PROFIT is hand-written in three live call sites, and the JS copy carries an extra fallback the two SQL copies do not (rule 14)
divergences.detail: The concept "an exchange's profit" has one named definition — `EXCHANGE_LEG_PROFIT` at packages/core/src/repositories/ProfitRepository.ts:884-885 — and three independent transcriptions: (1) ProfitRepository.ts:1851 and :2453 use the const; (2) ClosingRepository.ts:1318 inlines the identical SQL text verbatim, with a comment at :1302-1308 admitting the const is unexported and was copied rather than shared; (3) HistoryModal.tsx:387-390 is a JavaScript re-implementation that is NOT equivalent: it adds `: tx.profit_usd` as a fallback when BOTH leg columns are NULL, where both SQL copies COALESCE to 0. Also worth recording: migrations/index.ts:2896 and :2907 hold two frozen historical copies (v71 backfill) — harmless, but they are why nobody counted the live sites.
divergences.workedExample:
Take a hypothetical legacy row with leg1_profit_usd = NULL, leg2_profit_usd = NULL, profit_usd = 5.00:
  History modal (HistoryModal.tsx:387-390): condition (NULL !== null || NULL !== null) is false -> falls back to tx.profit_usd -> prints $5.00
  Profits (ProfitRepository.ts:884):        COALESCE(NULL,0) + COALESCE(NULL,0) = 0.00
  Closing (ClosingRepository.ts:1318):      COALESCE(NULL,0) + COALESCE(NULL,0) = 0.00
$5.00 vs $0.00 vs $0.00 for one row.
I could not find a way to produce such a row on current code: migration v30 backfilled `leg1_profit_usd = profit_usd WHERE leg1_rate IS NULL` (packages/core/src/db/migrations/index.ts:1517-1525), and every write path since validates `leg1ProfitUsd: z.number()` as required (packages/core/src/validators/exchange.ts:86) before ExchangeRepository.ts:305 writes it. So today the three copies return equal numbers — the finding is the drift surface, not a live wrong number. Any future change to what counts as exchange profit (e.g. netting a fee out of it, the way the MTC SMS fee is netted) has to be made in three files or it silently splits.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: ProfitRepository's named const. Export it (the closing arm's own comment at :1302-1308 says the only reason it was inlined was that the const is private) and have ClosingRepository import it; for the frontend, either send a server-computed profit field on the history row or mirror the SQL exactly (drop the profit_usd fallback).

divergences.title: The Dashboard's monthly net-profit tile omits exchange profit entirely while the Profits page includes it
divergences.surfaceB: dashboard monthly P&L tile (a sixth surface, outside the five)
divergences.detail: packages/core/src/repositories/FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL (:114-193) has exactly three arms — sales profit (:127-143), service commissions composed from ProfitRepository (:147-157), and expenses (:163-180) — and computes `netProfitUSD = salesResult.profit + commissionUsd - expenses_usd` (:184-185). There is no exchange arm; `grep -in exchange FinancialRepository.ts` returns only the method name line. Meanwhile ProfitService.getOverview folds `exchange.profit_usd` into `gross_profit_usd` and therefore into `net_profit_usd` (:477, :508-511), and getByDate folds `dex.profit_usd` into `net_profit_usd` (ProfitRepository.ts:2482-2484). The tile is consumed at frontend/src/features/dashboard/pages/Dashboard.tsx:388 + :396 (`monthlyNetProfitUSD: monthlyPL?.netProfitUSD`). Same omission applies to loto, custom services, maintenance and expenses-adjacent arms, but exchange is the one in scope here. This is the same class LIRA-159 fixed for commissions (that ticket replaced a raw SUM with composed ProfitRepository arms, doc comment at FinancialRepository.ts:60-77) — the composition just never reached exchange.
divergences.workedExample:
Suppose September holds nothing but ten LBP->USD exchanges of 9,000,000 LBP each, each stamping leg1_profit_usd = $0.5618, and no sales, commissions or expenses.

  Profits page, September, Overview: gross_profit_usd = 10 x 0.5618 = $5.62, net_profit_usd = $5.62 - $0 = $5.62
  Profits page, By Date, summed net_profit_usd over the month           = $5.62
  Dashboard monthly tile (FinancialRepository.ts:184): 0 (sales) + 0 (commission) - 0 (expenses) = $0.00

The operator sees $5.62 on one screen and $0.00 on the other for the same month and the same ten transactions. Add one $50 expense and the divergence flips sign on the Dashboard: Profits shows $5.62 - $50 = -$44.38, Dashboard shows -$50.00.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The Profits page. FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL should compose `ProfitRepository.getExchangeTotals(fromDt, toDt).profit_usd` the same way it already composes the two commission arms — its own docstring (:70-77) argues exactly that: a second definition of "profit recognised in this period" is the divergence class it set out to remove. It already imports `dateRange`/`monthBounds` so the window is identical.

result.notes:
WHAT IS ACTUALLY CLEAN — worth stating plainly, because most of this module is:

1. The dominant path (USD<->LBP, no lot, no partner) is byte-identical across preview, stamp, Profits and Closing. The preview total is `effectiveResult.totalProfitUsd`, submit sends that same value (index.tsx:951), `_applyExchangeLotEffects` returns `touched:false` for a USD/LBP pair before any rate lookup (ExchangeRepository.ts:686-689), so `exchange_transactions.profit_usd` and `transactions.profit_usd` are the previewed number unchanged. No MTC-style missing cost term exists on this path.

2. The frontend does NOT hand-roll the profit arithmetic. It imports `calculateExchange` and `computeOverrideLegProfitUsd` from @liratek/core (index.tsx:32-33) — the same functions the server-side `ExchangeService.addTransaction` would use. That is the single biggest reason exchange does not have the MTC bug: the formula genuinely has one owner (packages/core/src/utils/currencyConverter.ts).

3. The FIFO walker is shared: `consumeFifo` and `previewConsume` both delegate to one private walker (ExchangeLotRepository.ts:384-537, doc at :384-386). The lot-adjusted numbers are computed once and stamped on both the exchange row and the unified row from the same variable (ExchangeRepository.ts:342-357 then :408).

4. Dual-transport parity holds. Both electron-app/handlers/exchangeHandlers.ts:50 and backend/src/api/exchange.ts:70 call `ExchangeService.addDirectTransaction` against the one shared `exchangeSubmitSchema` (packages/core/src/validators/exchange.ts:78-95). `ExchangeService.addTransaction` (which recomputes from DB rates and would silently discard operator rate overrides) is now unreferenced by either transport — dead as a production path, but still exported and still a live footgun for a future caller.

5. Rule 20 is satisfied: TransactionRepository refuses to void an exchange whose lots are not reversible (`_assertExchangeLotsVoidable`, :1335-1338, :1571-1572) and restores FIFO consumption on both the refund and the void path (`_reverseExchangeLotEffects`, :1440, :1677). Profits and Closing both read `exchange_transactions.is_refunded`, so a reversed exchange drops out of both — no double-count, no orphan.

6. Closing's missing `notDebtPending` is a real non-issue, verified rather than assumed: ExchangeRepository.ts:504-513 hard-rejects any non-drawer payout method (`isDrawerAffectingMethod`), so an exchange can never write a CUSTOMER_ACCOUNT debt row. The comment at ClosingRepository.ts:1296-1301 is right about that half; it is wrong only about the partner half (divergence 2).

CAVEATS AND LIMITS OF THIS AUDIT:

- Everything above is source-read only, as instructed. I ran no tests and queried no database, so nothing here is confirmed against live rows. In particular I did not verify that any for-partner exchange with PARTIAL settlement coverage actually exists in the owner's DB — divergence 2 is proven reachable from code (PartnerRepository.applySettlementCoverage:424-469 writes partial `covered_amount`; ExchangeRepository.ts:576-593 books the FOR_EXCHANGE row) but its current live incidence is unknown.
- Divergence 3 (NO_RATE_ANCHOR) is the narrowest: it needs a cross where BOTH sides are non-LBP exotics with no `exchange_rates` row AND an operator rate override. I confirmed each precondition is individually reachable in the UI but did not confirm the owner actually trades such pairs.
- Divergence 1's severity assumes `formatAmount(row.revenue_usd, "USD")` renders a plain currency figure; I read the call site (Profits.tsx:1345) but not `formatAmount`'s body.
- Assumption (unverified): `getDecimals("EUR")` returns 2 in divergence 4's worked example. I traced the call (index.tsx:660-661, :685-686) but not the hook's table. The divergence exists for any non-zero rounding; only the exact cent figure depends on this.
- Surfaces I looked for and did NOT find: the Exchange page has no "today's profit" stats card (`getTodayStats`, ExchangeRepository.ts:975-1001, returns totalIn/totalOut/count only and has no renderer in the page). PositionsPanel's `unrealized_profit_usd` (ExchangeLotService.ts:222-246) is explicitly display-only and deliberately never reaches ProfitRepository — I do not count it as a divergence.
- One thing I noticed but did not chase because it is an amount, not a profit: `transactions.amount_usd` on an LBP->X or X->LBP cross exchange is overwritten with the leg-1 PROFIT rather than an amount (ExchangeRepository.ts:383 and :396, both self-documented as "informational"). Anything that sums `transactions.amount_usd` across types — the Transactions viewer's amount column and LIRA-139's amount sort — is reading a profit as a transaction size for those rows.

ProfitService then emits the by-module row with `revenue_usd: 0, cost_usd: 0, cost_lbp: 0, profit_usd: 0` HARDCODED (ProfitService.ts:626-630). getByUser/getByClient instead use the ungated generic arms: `ELSE t.profit_usd * txnPartnerCoverageRatio(t)` (:2844), `ELSE t.profit_lbp * txnPartnerCoverageRatio(t)` (:2860), and `SUM(t.amount_lbp) AS revenue_lbp` with no gate at all (:2817, :2973).
surfaces.currencies: LotoTotalsRow has NO usd field of any kind — revenue_lbp / profit_lbp / count only. transactions.profit_usd is never read by getLotoTotals or daily_loto. It IS read by getByUser/getByClient.

surfaces.location: packages/core/src/repositories/ClosingRepository.getDailyStatsSnapshot, loto arm at :1264-1284, folded into `totalProfitLBP` at :1360. Printed by frontend/src/features/closing/utils/closingReportGenerator.ts:117-122 via frontend/src/features/closing/utils/rateStampedProfit.ts, called from frontend/src/features/closing/pages/Checkpoint/index.tsx:311-330.
surfaces.formula: `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.profit_lbp),0) FROM loto_tickets lt JOIN transactions t ON t.source_table='loto_tickets' AND t.source_id=lt.id AND t.type='LOTO' WHERE t.status='ACTIVE' AND notRefunded(lt) AND notPartnerPending('loto_tickets','lt.id') AND notDebtPending(t.id) AND DATE(lt.created_at,'localtime')=DATE('now','localtime') AND tenant` — UNWEIGHTED sum, binary partner gate. Then `const totalProfitLBP = lotoProfit.profit_lbp;` (:1360) — loto is the ONLY contributor to totalProfitLBP. The PDF additionally converts it at sell_rate for the "Total (USD)" line (rateStampedProfit.ts:49-62, owner decision 2026-09-04).
surfaces.currencies: profit_lbp only. `totalProfitUSD` (:1329-1335) sums sales+fin+recharge+custom+maint+exchange and has NO loto term, so loto's stamped profit_usd never reaches the closing PDF.

divergences.title: Kept change (LBP) is in the transaction stamp and the Profits page but not in the Loto page's own Commission figures
divergences.surfaceA: table (Loto page "Commission" stat card + Ticket History "Commission" column)
divergences.detail: The stamp is `profit_lbp = commission_amount + kept_change_lbp` (packages/core/src/repositories/LotoTicketRepository.ts:190). Every downstream profit surface reads `t.profit_lbp` (ProfitRepository.ts:1792, :2428; ClosingRepository.ts:1272), so all three carry the kept change. The module's own surfaces read the `loto_tickets.commission_amount` COLUMN instead (LotoTicketRepository.ts:550 for the stat card; TicketHistoryModal.tsx:268 for the row), which is `sale_amount * commission_rate` and nothing else. Same shape as the MTC/SMS case, opposite sign: here the downstream surface ADDS a component the module page omits.
divergences.workedExample:
Ticket 500,000 LBP, rate 0.0445 -> commission 22,250 LBP. Customer hands 600,000 LBP cash; operator ticks "keep change" -> keptLbp = 100,000. Stamp: profit_lbp = 22,250 + 100,000 = 122,250.
  Loto page "Commission" card:        22,250 LBP
  Ticket History "Commission" column: 22,250 LBP
  Profits Overview "Loto Tickets":   122,250 LBP
  Closing PDF "LBP amount (Loto only)": 122,250 LBP
Two numbers, 100,000 LBP apart, for one sale.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp/Profits/Closing figure (122,250) is correct as PROFIT — the kept change is real money the drawer retained. The module page is correct as COMMISSION. The defect is that both are labelled "Commission" with no shared definition; rule 14 wants one named fragment for "loto profit" that both sides call, or the Loto page relabelled.

divergences.title: A for-partner ticket produces three different commission numbers: ungated on the Loto page, proportional on Profits, zero on the closing PDF
divergences.surfaceB: closing (notPartnerPending — binary) and table (no partner gate at all)
divergences.detail: getLotoTotals weights both monetary columns by `partnerCoverageRatio('loto_tickets','lt.id')` (ProfitRepository.ts:1791-1793, definition at :377-390). The closing arm still uses the binary `notPartnerPending('loto_tickets','lt.id')` (ClosingRepository.ts:1277, definition at ProfitRepository.ts:289-297) AND sums `t.profit_lbp` unweighted (:1272). `LotoTicketRepository.getTotalCommission:548-558` has no partner gate whatsoever. The split is deliberate — commit 5d61f9a4's message and docs/plans/todo_plans/PARTNER_PROPORTIONAL_RECOGNITION.md:5-7 both say "ClosingRepository keeps its binary gate" — but the closing arm's own comment at ClosingRepository.ts:1250-1253 still asserts it "mirrors ProfitRepository.getLotoTotals verbatim (same JOIN shape, same three gates it carries: notRefunded/notPartnerPending/notDebtPending)". getLotoTotals no longer carries notPartnerPending. The comment was true when written (LIRA-161, 2026-09-04, current_sprint.md:2754) and was falsified the next day by 5d61f9a4 without being updated. The FOR_LOTO ledger row it keys off is written at LotoTicketRepository.ts:370-380.
divergences.workedExample:
For-partner ticket, sale 1,000,000 LBP -> commission_amount 44,500 LBP, stamp profit_lbp 44,500. partner_ledger FOR_LOTO row: amount 1,000,000, covered_amount 400,000 -> ratio 0.4.
  Loto page "Commission" card:          44,500 LBP  (no partner gate)
  Ticket History "Commission" column:   44,500 LBP
  Profits By Module "Loto Tickets":     44,500 x 0.4 = 17,800 LBP profit, 400,000 LBP revenue
  Closing PDF "LBP amount (Loto only)": 0 LBP       (400,000 < 1,000,000 - 0.005 -> notPartnerPending is false, row dropped)
Three answers for one ticket: 44,500 / 17,800 / 0.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Profits (17,800) is authoritative for the Profits page — newest, owner-decided 2026-09-05. Closing (0) is authoritative for the closing PDF by the same decision (a same-day till-cash view). The Loto page's 44,500 has no recognition policy at all and is the one nobody chose. The actionable defect is the false comment at ClosingRepository.ts:1250-1253, which is exactly the trap that files a wrong finding later.

divergences.title: An on-account (CUSTOMER_ACCOUNT) ticket's commission is counted immediately on the Loto page but deferred everywhere else — and By Cashier shows its revenue with zero profit
divergences.surfaceA: table (Loto page Commission card, Ticket History)
divergences.detail: getLotoTotals carries `notDebtPending('t.id')` (ProfitRepository.ts:1798) and the closing arm carries it too (ClosingRepository.ts:1278); both defer the commission until the client repays (definition at ProfitRepository.ts:402-411, keyed on the 'Loto Debt' row written at LotoTicketRepository.ts:387-396). `getTotalCommission` (LotoTicketRepository.ts:548-558) has no such gate. Separately, getByUser/getByClient zero the PROFIT for a debt-pending row (`WHEN NOT notDebtPending(t.id) THEN 0`, ProfitRepository.ts:2793/2820/2848) but leave REVENUE completely ungated — `SUM(t.amount_lbp) AS revenue_lbp` at :2817 and :2973 has no debt gate, no partner weight, and no per-module CASE at all.
divergences.workedExample:
Ticket 500,000 LBP charged to client X's account -> commission 22,250 LBP, debt_ledger 'Loto Debt' 500,000 LBP with covered_lbp 0.
  Loto page "Commission" card:            22,250 LBP
  Ticket History "Commission" column:     22,250 LBP
  Profits By Module:                      no LOTO row at all (count 0 -> ProfitService.ts:622 skips it)
  Profits Overview "Loto Tickets" card:   not rendered (Profits.tsx:1039 gates on count > 0)
  Profits By Cashier row:                 profit 0 / $0.00, but revenue_lbp 500,000 LBP
  Closing PDF "LBP amount (Loto only)":   0 LBP
The By Cashier tab therefore reports 500,000 LBP of loto revenue for a period in which the By Module tab reports that loto did not exist.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The deferred treatment (0 until repaid) is the owner-decided DBT-1 policy and is correct for the Profits/Closing surfaces. The Loto page's 22,250 is a raw column sum with no policy. getByUser/getByClient's raw `SUM(t.amount_lbp)` revenue is the clearest outright bug of the three — it applies a debt gate to profit and none to revenue in the same SELECT.

divergences.title: Loto's stamped profit_usd (kept USD change) is real money that reaches exactly one screen and reads as $0 on the other three
divergences.surfaceA: profits By Cashier / By Client tabs
divergences.surfaceB: profits Overview + By Module, and closing
divergences.detail: The stamp writes `profit_usd: data.kept_change_usd ?? 0` (LotoTicketRepository.ts:189) and kept change is emitted per TENDER currency, so a USD-tendered loto ticket produces a USD figure (MultiPaymentInput.tsx:1116-1131). `LotoTotalsRow` (ProfitRepository.ts:87) has no USD field and getLotoTotals never selects `t.profit_usd` (:1790-1793); neither does the `daily_loto` CTE (:2427-2428). ProfitService then hardcodes `revenue_usd: 0` / `profit_usd: 0` on the by-module row (ProfitService.ts:626, :630), and only adds `loto.profit_lbp` to grossProfitLbp (:488) — loto contributes nothing to grossProfitUsd (:470-481). ClosingRepository's totalProfitUSD (:1329-1335) likewise has no loto term. But getByUser/getByClient fall to the generic `ELSE t.profit_usd * txnPartnerCoverageRatio(t)` arm (ProfitRepository.ts:2844) because loto matches neither the `financial_services` nor the `sales` branch, and Profits.tsx:1725 renders it.
divergences.workedExample:
Ticket 500,000 LBP; buy rate 90,000 so the ticket is $5.5556. Customer hands $6. Change $0.4444; operator ticks "keep change" -> keptUsd = 0.4444, keptLbp = 0. Stamp: profit_usd = 0.4444, profit_lbp = 22,250.
  Profits Overview "Loto Tickets" card:  22,250 LBP, no USD line exists (Profits.tsx:1049-1061)
  Profits By Module LOTO row:            Profit (USD) $0.00 (hardcoded), Profit (LBP) 22,250
  Profits By Cashier row:                profit_usd includes $0.44
  Closing PDF "USD amount":              $0.00 contribution from loto
Over 200 such tickets that is ~$89 of stamped profit visible on one tab and $0 on the other three.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp is authoritative — the drawer physically holds those dollars. Every loto-specific reader (getLotoTotals, daily_loto, the closing arm) was written on the assumption 'loto is LBP-only', which is true of the commission but NOT of the stamp once T3 keep-change was wired into this form. getLotoTotals should return a profit_usd and ProfitService should stop hardcoding 0.

divergences.title: The By Module "Margin" column divides LOTO's two hardcoded zeros and therefore always prints 0%
divergences.surfaceB: the same row's own Profit (LBP) / Revenue (LBP) cells
divergences.detail: The Margin cell is `formatPct(row.profit_usd, row.revenue_usd)` (frontend/src/features/profits/pages/Profits.tsx:1356) and `formatPct` returns the literal string "0%" when the denominator is 0 (Profits.tsx:291-294). ProfitService emits the LOTO row with `revenue_usd: 0` and `profit_usd: 0` hardcoded (ProfitService.ts:626, :630) because loto is LBP-denominated. So the Margin column for LOTO is structurally incapable of showing anything but 0%, even though the row directly to its left shows a non-zero LBP revenue and profit. This is the exact second class named in the audit brief — a percentage computed from the USD columns while the money is in LBP.
divergences.workedExample:
One month, 100 tickets at 500,000 LBP each, no partner/debt cases.
  revenue_lbp = 50,000,000 LBP
  profit_lbp  = 100 x 22,250 = 2,225,000 LBP
  true margin = 2,225,000 / 50,000,000 = 4.45%
  Margin column renders: formatPct(0, 0) -> "0%"
The operator reads "Loto Tickets ... 0%" on a row that simultaneously shows 2,225,000 LBP of profit.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The LBP cells are correct; the Margin cell is wrong. Fix is a per-currency margin (or profit_lbp/revenue_lbp when the USD pair is empty), not a change to the data.

divergences.title: sale_date vs created_at: a backdated ticket appears on the Loto page today and on the Profits page on a different day
divergences.surfaceA: table (Loto page Commission card, Ticket History source query, Settlement Verification) — filters `date(sale_date)`
divergences.detail: The form always sends `sale_date: localDay()` — today, computed in the browser, never derived from the Transaction Time override (frontend/src/features/loto/pages/Loto/index.tsx:262 vs the separate `transaction_time: transactionTime` at :298). The repository writes `created_at` from that override (`COALESCE(?, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)`, LotoTicketRepository.ts:143 with `data.transaction_time` as the bound param at :160), and the service explicitly permits any past timestamp (LotoService.ts:145-153). Every module-side query then filters `date(sale_date)` (LotoTicketRepository.ts:539, :551, :563, :585, :461) while every profit-side query filters `lt.created_at` (ProfitRepository.ts:1799 via dateRange, :2426/:2434; ClosingRepository.ts:1279 via todayLocal).
divergences.workedExample:
On 2026-09-06 the operator sells a 500,000 LBP ticket (commission 22,250) and sets Transaction Time to 2026-09-01 14:00.
  Row: created_at = 2026-09-01 14:00, sale_date = '2026-09-06'.
  Loto page Commission card on 2026-09-06:  22,250 LBP
  Loto page report for 2026-09-01:          0
  Profits page for 2026-09-06:              0
  Profits page for 2026-09-01:              22,250 LBP
  Closing snapshot on 2026-09-06:           0  (todayLocal(created_at) misses)
  Closing snapshot for 2026-09-01:          already taken before the row existed -> the 22,250 reaches NO closing snapshot ever.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: created_at is authoritative — it is the column the operator's own override sets, and it is what every other module's profit query uses. sale_date being pinned to `localDay()` at submit time is the bug: it ignores the override the same form collects three lines later.

divergences.title: The "Unchecked Activity" panel re-implements "uncheckpointed" with the date-range logic the backend explicitly abandoned as buggy, and without the refund gate
divergences.surfaceB: the checkpoint that the panel's own button creates (LotoService.createCheckpoint)
divergences.detail: The panel computes its ticket set as `api.loto.getByDateRange(periodStart, today)` where periodStart = last checkpoint's period_end + 1 day (frontend/src/features/loto/components/SettlementVerification.tsx:121-134), then sums `commission_amount` client-side (:137-140). The server sweep the "Create Checkpoint for These Sales" button triggers (:629 -> LotoService.createCheckpoint:622-623) uses `checkpoint_id IS NULL` and carries `notRefunded` (LotoTicketRepository.getUncheckpointedTotals:657-666). LotoService.ts:620-621 names the difference in a comment: "Use checkpoint_id IS NULL to find uncheckpointed items — This avoids the date-range bug when two checkpoints happen on the same day." The frontend still has that bug. Additionally `getTicketsByDateRange` (LotoTicketRepository.ts:458-465) deliberately carries NO is_refunded gate, so the panel counts voided tickets. The Loto page's own header Checkpoint button uses the correct server call (index.tsx:181) — only this panel diverges.
divergences.workedExample:
Case A (the named date-range bug). Checkpoint C1 created today, period_end = '2026-09-06'. Then a 300,000 LBP ticket is sold (commission 13,350, checkpoint_id NULL).
  Panel: periodStart = '2026-09-07'; getByDateRange('2026-09-07','2026-09-06') -> `date(sale_date) BETWEEN '2026-09-07' AND '2026-09-06'` -> 0 rows -> the Unchecked Activity card does not render at all (guard at :158).
  Server: getUncheckpointedTotals -> count 1, commission 13,350 LBP.
  Panel says "nothing pending"; 13,350 LBP of commission is pending.

Case B (refunds). No checkpoint yet (periodStart '1970-01-01'). Two tickets today, 500,000 LBP each; one is later voided.
  Panel: sales 1,000,000, commission 44,500, weOweLoto = 1,000,000 - 44,500 = 955,500 -> renders "We pay LOTO 955,500 LBP".
  Checkpoint actually created: total_sales 500,000, total_commission 22,250 -> weOweLoto 477,750.
  The preview overstates the settlement by exactly 477,750 LBP.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The server (checkpoint_id IS NULL + notRefunded) is authoritative and says so in its own comment. The panel should call `api.loto.getUncheckpointed()` — which already exists and is already what index.tsx:181 uses — instead of re-deriving the set from dates.

divergences.title: The Dashboard's Monthly Net Profit (LBP) has no loto arm, so loto's entire profit is zero there while it is the whole of the closing PDF's LBP profit
divergences.detail: packages/core/src/repositories/FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL:114-198 composes exactly three arms — sale_items margin (:126-140, USD only), financial-service commission via getRealizedCommissionTotals + getSupplierCommissionTotals (:145-149), and expenses (:160-175). There is no loto term anywhere in the method (grep for "loto" in FinancialRepository.ts returns nothing), so `netProfitLBP = commissionLbp - expensesLBP` (:180) can never contain a loto figure. Rendered at frontend/src/features/dashboard/pages/Dashboard.tsx:396-397 and :853-857. This is the same money that ClosingRepository.ts:1360 makes the SOLE content of totalProfitLBP.
divergences.workedExample:
A month whose only activity is 100 loto tickets at 500,000 LBP each (commission 22,250 each), plus zero expenses.
  Profits page, month range, gross_profit_lbp:      2,225,000 LBP
  Sum of that month's closing PDFs, "LBP amount":   2,225,000 LBP
  Dashboard "Monthly Net Profit" LBP tile:          0 LBP
The shop's entire month of loto profit reads as zero on the Dashboard.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Profits/Closing are authoritative — loto profit is real and already stamped. getMonthlyPL is an omission, structurally the same class LIRA-159 fixed for financial-service commission (it composed the gated ProfitRepository arms instead of a raw SUM) but never extended to loto.

divergences.title: The same loto ticket stamps exchange_rate 100,000 sold directly and the session's operator rate sold through a basket
divergences.detail: `lotoSellSchema` (packages/core/src/validators/loto.ts:15-49) has no `exchange_rate` key, so zod strips whatever the caller sends and the repository falls to its hardcoded default: `exchange_rate: data.exchange_rate ?? 100000` (LotoTicketRepository.ts:191). The session path never passes through that schema — SessionCheckoutService.processCartItem injects the live rate (`if (data.exchange_rate === undefined) data.exchange_rate = exchangeRate`, packages/core/src/services/SessionCheckoutService.ts:121-124) and calls `lotoService.sellTicket(data as never)` directly (:185). The stamped rate is what the Transactions viewer's Amount column converts by, at each row's OWN stamped rate (frontend/src/features/audit/amountSort.ts:24-27).
divergences.workedExample:
Two identical 500,000 LBP loto tickets on the same day, live buy rate 90,000.
  Sold from the Loto page directly: transactions.exchange_rate = 100,000 -> Amount-column sort value 500,000 / 100,000 = $5.00
  Sold inside a session basket:     transactions.exchange_rate = 90,000  -> sort value 500,000 / 90,000  = $5.56
The two rows sort as if they were worth different amounts, and any future per-row rate-stamped conversion (the pattern rateStampedProfit.ts:71-83 says it could not use here only because the closing snapshot returns bucketed SUMs) would convert them differently.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The session path (real operator rate) is correct. 100,000 is a placeholder that predates the rate table and is now the only rate a directly-sold loto ticket ever gets. No displayed money figure changes today — this is sort order and a latent trap, not a wrong printed number, so it ranks below the seven above.

divergences.title: 0.0445 is hardcoded in five production places; the frontend copy can override the shop's configured rate when the settings fetch fails
divergences.detail: Rule 14 — the commission rate has one meaning and six literals: frontend/src/features/loto/pages/Loto/index.tsx:111, packages/core/src/services/LotoService.ts:454 and :460, packages/core/src/repositories/LotoTicketRepository.ts:150 and :202, plus the seeds at packages/core/src/db/migrations/index.ts:1841/:1875 and packages/core/src/repositories/TenantRepository.ts:624. They agree today, so there is no live numeric divergence. The live risk is one-directional: the page ALWAYS sends `commission_rate` (index.tsx:260), it IS in the schema (validators/loto.ts:30), and LotoService takes the sent value in preference to settings (`data.commission_rate ?? this.getCommissionRate()`, LotoService.ts:156). `loadSettings()` swallows every failure silently (index.tsx:130-134), leaving `settings` null and `commissionRate` at the literal 0.0445.
divergences.workedExample:
Owner raises the loto commission to 5% in settings. On a client where the settings fetch failed (any thrown error — the catch at index.tsx:132-134 is empty and the form stays fully usable), a 500,000 LBP ticket is sold:
  page sends commission_rate: 0.0445
  LotoService honours the sent value, never reads settings -> commission_amount = 22,250 LBP
  correct value at the configured 5%             -> 25,000 LBP
  shortfall 2,750 LBP per ticket, and every surface then agrees on the wrong number (they all read the stored column or the stamp), so nothing on screen contradicts it.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The settings row is authoritative. Two fixes, either sufficient: stop sending `commission_rate` from the page (the server already defaults from settings), or surface the settings-load failure instead of swallowing it. Marked userVisible because the number the operator is billed on is wrong, but it requires the settings fetch to have failed — I did not reproduce that precondition.

result.notes:
SURFACE 1 DOES NOT EXIST — that is itself the first finding. The Loto sell form never shows the operator a commission figure before submit. `commissionAmount` is computed (index.tsx:112-114) and put in the payload (:261), but it is stripped by zod (`lotoSellSchema` has no such key) and recomputed server-side (LotoService.ts:157). So there is no MTC-shaped preview-vs-stamp bug here for the simple reason that there is no preview; the nearest thing the operator sees is the header "Commission" stat card, which is today's TOTAL, not this ticket's. Note the asymmetry though: `commission_rate` IS accepted from the client (validators/loto.ts:30) and takes precedence over settings — see the last divergence.

WHAT IS GENUINELY CLEAN. getLotoTotals (ProfitRepository.ts:1787-1808) and the `daily_loto` CTE (:2424-2437) are byte-for-byte the same query modulo the GROUP BY — same partnerCoverageRatio weighting, same three gates, same date column. The Profits Overview card and the By Module row both come from that single method through ProfitService (:407 and :621), so they cannot disagree. LOTO_CASH_PRIZE, LOTO_MONTHLY_FEE and LOTO_SETTLEMENT stamp no profit at all (LotoCashPrizeRepository.ts:79-93, LotoMonthlyFeeRepository.ts:101-115, LotoCheckpointRepository.ts:278-296) and none of those types is in PROFIT_TXN_TYPES (ProfitRepository.ts:953-954), so there is no double-count between the sale and its settlement. The refund path negates both profit columns symmetrically (TransactionRepository.ts:1613-1633).

TWO THINGS I FOUND BUT DID NOT FILE AS DIVERGENCES, because no two surfaces disagree — every surface omits them identically:
- The loto MONTHLY FEE is a genuine cost that reaches no profit surface at all. It debits the drawer (LotoMonthlyFeeRepository.ts:107,117-120) and lands in `loto_monthly_fees`, not `expenses`, so `activeExpense`-gated expense arms never see it. The module's own settlement math DOES subtract it ("We owe LOTO: sales minus our commission, plus any fees", LotoService.ts:326,338) — so the loto settlement view and every profit view disagree about whether the fee is a cost, but the profit views are uniformly silent, not inconsistent with each other.
- `notRefunded` (retroactive removal, used by getLotoTotals) versus REFUND-row netting (used by getByUser/getByClient) gives different answers when the sale and its refund fall in different reporting periods. This is a documented app-wide pattern (ProfitRepository.ts:1817-1823 spells out the same tradeoff for PM fees), not loto-specific, so I left it out.

ONE COSMETIC BUG NOT WORTH A TICKET ON ITS OWN: TicketHistoryModal's Date column declares `sortKey: "sale_date"` (:171) but renders `created_at` (:218-223). With the sale_date/created_at split described in divergence 6, a backdated ticket displays one date and sorts by another.

METHOD / CONFIDENCE. Every file:line above was read in this session and re-checked with `sed -n` after drafting; none is quoted from a comment. Where a comment and the code disagreed I trusted the code and said so — ClosingRepository.ts:1250-1253's "mirrors getLotoTotals verbatim ... notPartnerPending" is false as of commit 5d61f9a4, which is precisely the class of stale cite the brief warned about. The one claim I could NOT execute against a live database is the SQLite behaviour of the inverted `BETWEEN '2026-09-07' AND '2026-09-06'` range in divergence 7 case A; I am reading it from the SQL text (LotoTicketRepository.ts:461) plus the backend's own comment naming that exact failure (LotoService.ts:620-621), and standard SQL semantics make an inverted BETWEEN match nothing. Likely, on that basis: zero rows. The refund half of that same divergence (case B) needs no such inference and stands on its own. I also did not verify divergence 10's precondition (a real settings-fetch failure) — the code path is plainly there, but I did not reproduce it. I ran no tests, builds or package commands, and made no edits.

result.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — I attempted refutation and every check upheld the claim.

INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION (different route): rather than repeat the claimant's symbolic arithmetic, I built a minimal sales/sale_items schema in a real SQLite engine (Python stdlib sqlite3 — no better-sqlite3 ABI coupling) and executed all five expressions verbatim, including the inlined saleFullyPaid/saleRecognitionWeight fragments. Results: stamp=12.00, ProfitRepo rev-cost (:1268/9)=12.00 (rev=30.0, cost=18.0), ProfitRepo :3066=12.00, Closing :871=4.00, FinancialRepo :130=4.00, chart :1999=4.00. Both claimed answers reproduce exactly; the $8.00 / 67% under-report is correct.

UNIT-VS-LINE-TOTAL SEMANTICS proven three ways WITHOUT relying on the claimant's cite. (1) Conservation: sold_price_usd*quantity = 10*3 = $30 = sales.final_amount_usd = cash tendered; if it were a line total the product would be $90 and would not reconcile. (2) cost_price_snapshot_usd is bound from (SELECT cost_price_usd FROM products …) at SalesRepository.ts:766 — unambiguously a unit cost. (3) SalesRepository.ts:1399 `refundAmount = item.sold_price_usd * params.refundQuantity` is only coherent per-unit. Schema confirms quantity is its own column: electron-app/create_db.sql:369-371.

result.correction:
The claim stands as filed — arithmetic, magnitude, line cites, authority and consumer surfaces all verified. Three refinements worth folding into the ticket, none of which change the conclusion:

1. SCOPE LIMIT THE CLAIMANT OMITTED (most important). IMEI/unit-tracked lines are hard-pinned to quantity = 1 by a BusinessRuleError at packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:854 ("unit-tracked lines are one-unit-per-line"), so phone sales cannot trigger this. The divergence bites only non-unit-tracked stock — accessories, cases, consumables — which is exactly the worked example. This narrows blast radius (and likely explains why it went unnoticed: the highest-value SKUs are immune) but does not affect the arithmetic.

2. A FOURTH AUTHORITY SITE THE CLAIMANT MISSED, which strengthens the case: the refund reversal at packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:1413-1414 computes `(item.sold_price_usd - item.cost_price_snapshot_usd) * params.refundQuantity`. So the tally is 4 quantity-carrying sites vs 3 bare — and it means a refund's NEGATIVE stamp is quantity-scaled while closing's POSITIVE is not, so a fully-refunded multi-unit line drives the closing/monthly/chart figures NEGATIVE rather than to zero. Worked example: the 3-unit line fully refunded contributes +4.00 at sale and -12.00 at refund on those three surfaces, netting -8.00 where it must net 0. That is a second, arguably worse, symptom worth naming in the ticket.

3. TWO MINOR CITE LOOSENESSES. (a) "proven at SalesRepository.ts:901-911" — :901-909 is the .run() binding; the INSERT column list that actually establishes the ordering is at :763-767, and the cost binding is the subquery at :766. Cite both. (b) Dashboard.tsx:1289 is the `{ value: "Profit", label: "Profit" }` select option, not the chart render; the load call is :383.

Suggested fix direction (all three sites take `* si.quantity`), with the rule-14 observation that this is precisely the copy-paste-a-predicate failure mode rule 14 exists to prevent: the sales-margin expression should be ONE named fragment beside saleFullyPaid/notRefunded in ProfitRepository.ts's rule-14 block and reused, not a seventh hand-written copy. Per rule 17, prove any guard test fails on the pre-fix code first.

divergences.title: Post-cutover OMT/WHISH revenue is counted in the Profits Overview but is invisible in the By-Date tab until the row is supplier-settled
divergences.detail: ProfitService.getSummary adds BOTH arms into one `finSvc.revenue_*`: the settled arm (ProfitRepository.getFinancialSettledByCurrency, `fs.is_settled = 1`) at ProfitService.ts:305-311 AND the pending arm (getFinancialPendingByCurrency, `fs.is_settled = 0`) at ProfitService.ts:316-326 (`finSvc.revenue_lbp += row.revenue` / `finSvc.revenue_usd += row.revenue`). getByDate's `daily_commissions` CTE has only ONE base arm and it requires `fs.is_settled = 1` (ProfitRepository.ts:2357); its allocation arm (:2260-2276) contributes `0 AS revenue_usd, 0 AS revenue_lbp`. Since LIRA-158's D3 cutover every OMT/WHISH SEND/RECEIVE is born `commission_model = 1` and therefore `is_settled = 0` (isPendingSupplierSettlement, FinancialServiceRepository.ts:877-880, called at :1573), so this is the normal case, not an edge case.
divergences.workedExample: Today, one OMT INTRA SEND: amount $200.00 USD, omt_fee $3.00. financial_services row: amount = 200, cost = 0, price = 0, commission_model = 1, is_settled = 0. fsRevenue(fs) = `CASE WHEN cost > 0 THEN price ELSE amount END` = 200.  Profits -> Overview, financial_services Revenue (Profits.tsx:793, via ProfitService.ts:322): $200.00, and gross_revenue_usd includes it.  Profits -> By Date, today's row, Revenue column (ProfitRepository.ts:2357 excludes is_settled = 0): $0.00.  Same page, same period, two tabs: $200.00 versus $0.00. It appears in the By-Date tab retroactively, on its own transaction date, only after the OMT batch is settled days later.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Undecided without the owner — this is a recognition question, not a typo. The Overview counting unsettled revenue is defensible (the transfer really happened); the By-Date tab excluding it is defensible (cash basis). What is NOT defensible is the same page answering "what was our revenue on 2026-09-06" two different ways. Whichever basis wins, both arms must share one named predicate (rule 14) — there is no fragment for "a financial-service row's revenue is recognised when..." today, only two inline `fs.is_settled` tests.

divergences.title: Profits Overview "Commission" reads the transaction stamp (kept change included, no model gate); the By-Payment-Method "Commission (Settled)" row reads the fs.commission column (kept change excluded, model-0 only, no provider filter)
divergences.detail: Two expressions for one concept on one page. ProfitRepository.getFinancialSettledByCurrency:1565 sums `CASE WHEN fs.currency = 'LBP' THEN t.profit_lbp ELSE t.profit_usd END` — the STAMP, which FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1971/1977 defines as `commission + kept_change`, and which carries no `embeddedCommission` gate (it does not need one, because the stamp is already 0 for model-1) but IS restricted to `fs.provider IN COMMISSION_PROVIDERS` (:1571). ProfitRepository.getRealizedCommissionTotals:2579-2580 sums `fs.commission` — the COLUMN, no kept change — gated by `fs.commission > 0` and `embeddedCommission(fs)` (:2585-2586) but with NO provider restriction at all, so it also sweeps in iPick/Katsh/BOB cost-price margins (`commission = price - cost`, FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1496-1497), which the Overview deliberately routes to a separate mobile_services block (ProfitService.ts:349-372). Same underlying money, two hand-written definitions.
divergences.workedExample: One OMT_APP USD RECEIVE today: fee $1.00, commission_model = 0, is_settled = 1, and the operator keeps $0.25 of the customer's change (OmtWhishAppTransferForm.tsx:427-433 sends kept_change_usd = 0.25).  fs.commission = 1.00; transactions.profit_usd = 1.00 + 0.25 = 1.25 (FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1966-1971).  Profits -> Overview, financial_services Commission (ProfitRepository.ts:1565): $1.25.  Profits -> By Payment Method, "Commission (Settled)" row (ProfitRepository.ts:2579, via ProfitService.ts:723): $1.00.  $0.25 apart. Add one Katsh catalog item sold today at cost 100,000 / price 130,000 LBP (model 0, is_settled 1, commission = 30,000) and the gap widens: By-Payment-Method's Commission row also picks up 30,000 LBP that the Overview reports under Mobile Services instead.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The Overview (stamp-based) is the better source — the stamp is what every other module reports and what void/refund reverses. getRealizedCommissionTotals additionally feeds the Dashboard "Monthly Net Profit" tile (FinancialRepository.ts:146), so the divergence escapes the Profits page. Either way rule 14 wants one named fragment for "financial-service commission recognised in period"; there are currently three (this one, the stamp arm, and Closing's own `CASE WHEN currency != 'LBP' THEN commission`).

divergences.title: By-Module "Margin" column divides the USD columns only, so every LBP-denominated OMT/Whish provider row reads 0%
divergences.detail: frontend/src/features/profits/pages/Profits.tsx:1356 renders `formatPct(row.profit_usd, row.revenue_usd)` for a table whose two adjacent columns are "Revenue (LBP)" (:1327-1330) and "Profit (LBP)" (:1344-1351). formatPct (:291-294) returns the literal string "0%" when `total === 0`. The rows come from ProfitService.getByModule -> getFinancialSettledByProvider (ProfitRepository.ts:2101), which correctly splits revenue_usd/revenue_lbp and profit_usd/profit_lbp (:2142-2145). This is the exact second defect class named in the audit brief — a percentage computed from the wrong currency's columns — reproduced here for the financial-services provider rows.
divergences.workedExample: Period contains only LBP OMT_APP activity: five legacy RECEIVEs totalling 4,500,000 LBP of amount with 45,000 LBP of fees. getFinancialSettledByProvider returns for provider OMT_APP: revenue_usd = 0, revenue_lbp = 4,500,000, profit_usd = 0, profit_lbp = 45,000, count = 5.  By-Module row renders: Revenue (USD) $0.00 | Revenue (LBP) 4,500,000 | Profit (USD) $0.00 | Profit (LBP) 45,000 | Count 5 | Margin "0%" (formatPct(0, 0)).  True margin: 45,000 / 4,500,000 = 1.0%. The row shows real money in two columns and 0% in the third.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The SQL is right; the renderer is wrong. Correct margin needs one of: per-currency margin (two values), or a single margin over USD-equivalents converted at a stated rate. The latter needs an owner decision on which rate — note LIRA-174 already resolved the analogous question for the closing PDF as `sell_rate`, deliberately diverging from the app-wide buy-rate convention (docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md "Owner decisions recorded today"), so this should not be guessed.

divergences.title: getAnalytics buckets "today"/"this month" by the UTC date of created_at while every other reporting query converts to local time first — rows created between midnight and 03:00 Beirut are never counted
divergences.detail: FinancialServiceRepository.getAnalytics uses `DATE(created_at) = DATE('now', 'localtime')` (:4728, :4746, :4793) and `strftime('%Y-%m', created_at) = strftime('%Y-%m', 'now', 'localtime')` (:4760, :4778) — the LEFT side has no `'localtime'` modifier, so a UTC date/month is compared against a local one. `financial_services.created_at` defaults to SQLite's `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, which is UTC (FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1747). Every sibling surface converts the column: ClosingRepository's `todayLocal` = `DATE(col, 'localtime') = DATE('now', 'localtime')` (:56-57), ProfitRepository's `dateRange` = `datetime(col, 'localtime') >= ? AND <= ?` (:668), SalesRepository.ts:1627/1639/1651/1661. ClosingRepository's own todayLocal doc comment (:49-51) even claims it "Mirrors the convention used across ... FinancialServiceRepository" — that claim is false for this method. Beirut is UTC+3, so the mismatch window is the first three hours of every local day.
divergences.workedExample: An OMT_APP RECEIVE entered at 01:30 on Sat 2026-09-06 Beirut time. created_at is stored '2026-09-05 22:30:00' UTC. fee $5.00, commission_model = 0, is_settled = 1.  Services page "Today" chip and Profits -> Commissions "Realized Commissions (Today)" (getAnalytics:4728): DATE('2026-09-05 22:30:00') = '2026-09-05' versus DATE('now','localtime') = '2026-09-06' -> excluded -> $0.00. It is excluded on 2026-09-06 for the whole day, and it did not exist during 2026-09-05's local day, so it is counted on NO day.  Profits -> Overview with the date picker on 2026-09-06 (ProfitRepository.dateRange:668): datetime('2026-09-05 22:30:00','localtime') = '2026-09-06 01:30:00', inside ['2026-09-06 00:00:00','2026-09-06 23:59:59'] -> included -> $5.00.  Same transaction, same day: $0.00 versus $5.00. The month variants at :4760/:4778 do the same thing across a month boundary (a 01:00 1-Sep entry is counted in August).
divergences.suspectedAuthority: ProfitRepository/ClosingRepository/SalesRepository — the `'localtime'` form is the repo-wide convention and the documented one. getAnalytics is the single outlier. Caveat worth naming: HANDOVER_2026-09-04 trap #5 records that SQLite's `'localtime'` and JS `Date` disagree by two hours on Windows under `TZ=Asia/Beirut` in core jest (LIRA-168), so a fixture-backed test for this must pin the boundary in UTC rather than trust either side's local rendering.

divergences.title: OMT App / Whish App payment sheet shows the GROSS "Shop Profit" while the discount input on the same sheet reduces the submitted commission
divergences.detail: frontend/src/features/recharge/components/OmtWhishAppTransferForm.tsx:1137-1144 passes `{ label: "Shop Profit", value: formatAmount(shopProfit, currency) }` into PaymentSheet's `summary` prop, and :1162-1164 passes `showDiscount={true}` / `maxDiscount={shopProfit}` / `onDiscountChange={setDiscount}` to the SAME sheet. PaymentSheet.tsx:214-230 renders the summary block and :234-272 renders MultiPaymentInput (which owns the discount field) inside one scrolling body — both visible at once. But the submitted commission at :355 is `Math.max(0, shopProfit - discount)`, and the fee-breakdown panel above the sheet (:826-831) is also gross. Nothing on screen ever shows the post-discount figure. The stamp then writes `profit_usd/profit_lbp = commission + kept_change` (FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1966-1979; OMT_APP/WHISH_APP are commission_model = 0 because isOmtWhishTransfer requires provider exactly 'OMT'/'WHISH', :864-869), so the discounted value is what every downstream surface reports.
divergences.workedExample: WHISH_APP RECEIVE, USD, amount $100.00. Auto fee = 1% = $1.00 (omtWhishAppFees.ts:69-74), shopProfit = providerFee = $1.00 (:105). The operator grants a $0.40 discount in the payment sheet.  Payment sheet summary line, "Shop Profit" (OmtWhishAppTransferForm.tsx:1142): "$1.00".  Submitted commission (:355): max(0, 1.00 - 0.40) = $0.60.  transactions.profit_usd (FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1971): $0.60.  Services history Profit column and Profits Overview: $0.60.  The confirm screen promises $1.00 of profit on the same panel where the operator gives $0.40 of it away.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp. The summary line should read `formatAmount(Math.max(0, shopProfit - discount), currency)` — `discount` is already in scope at that point (state declared :146, wired :1164). Low blast radius, one expression.

divergences.title: An LBP OMT App / Whish App transfer inside a customer session contributes zero session profit
divergences.detail: OmtWhishAppTransferForm.tsx:441-449 calls linkTransaction with `amountUsd: currency === "USD" ? totalAmount : 0, amountLbp: currency === "LBP" ? totalAmount : 0, profitUsd: currency === "USD" ? Math.max(0, shopProfit - discount) : 0` — the amount is currency-branched but the profit is not: there is no `profitLbp` argument at all. The field exists and is supported end to end: frontend/src/api/backendApi.ts:3157 declares `profitLbp?: number`, and CustomerSessionRepository.linkTransaction:274-291 takes `profitLbp: number = 0` and INSERTs it into `session_transactions.profit_lbp`, which CustomerSessionRepository.ts:397-398 sums as `total_profit_lbp`. So for an LBP transfer the session ledger silently records 0 while transactions.profit_lbp records the real figure.
divergences.workedExample: Whish App RECEIVE inside an active customer session: currency LBP, amount 9,000,000 LBP, manual fee 90,000 LBP, no discount. shopProfit = 90,000 LBP.  Transaction stamp (FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1977, commission_model = 0 for WHISH_APP): profit_lbp = 90,000.  Profits Overview financial_services.commission_lbp: 90,000 LBP.  Session link (OmtWhishAppTransferForm.tsx:446-447): profitUsd = 0 (currency is not USD), profitLbp not passed -> defaults to 0.  session_transactions.profit_lbp = 0; the session's total_profit_lbp gains nothing.  90,000 LBP versus 0 for the same transaction.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp. The fix is one added line mirroring the amountLbp branch: `profitLbp: currency === "LBP" ? Math.max(0, shopProfit - discount) : 0`. Confidence note: I verified the argument list, the adapter's declared shape and the repository's INSERT, but did not run the session-summary path end to end, so "the session card shows 0" is a derivation from those three, not an observed screen.

divergences.title: The Services page hand-copies the OMT commission rates and both fee tier tables out of packages/core — equal today, unlinked (rule 14)
divergences.detail: frontend/src/features/services/pages/Services/index.tsx:65-124 declares its own `OMT_COMMISSION_RATES`, `INTRA_FEE_TIERS`, `WESTERN_UNION_FEE_TIERS`, `INTRA_LBP_MAX_AMOUNT`, `lookupIntraLbpFee`, `lookupOmtFee` and `WHISH_FEE_TIERS`, each carrying a `// must match omtFees.ts` / `// must match whishFees.ts` comment as the only link. The authoritative definitions are packages/core/src/utils/omtFees.ts:26-34 (rates), :50-63 (INTRA tiers), :74-77 (lookupIntraLbpFee), :82-90 (Western Union tiers), :117-142 (lookupOmtFee), and the stamp path calls them through calculateCommission (omtFees.ts:158-172, invoked at FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1345/1352/1362/1389). I compared every value: they agree today. Two structural differences that are latent, not yet live: the frontend copy omits `OMT_WALLET: 0.001` and `ONLINE_BROKERAGE: 0.0` entirely and falls back to `?? 0` (:1897), which is harmless only because the preview block is gated to exclude those two service types (:1877-1879); and core rounds via `Number((omtFee * rate).toFixed(4))` while the frontend does a bare `feeVal * rate` then rounds at render.
divergences.workedExample: No arithmetic divergence exists today — this is the drift channel, not a live wrong number, and I am reporting it as such rather than inventing one. The failure it will produce: change CASH_TO_BUSINESS from 0.25 to 0.20 in omtFees.ts:29 and nothing else. Backend stamp for a $40 CASH_TO_BUSINESS fee: calculateCommission -> 40 x 0.20 = $8.00, written to fs.commission and (for a model-0 row) transactions.profit_usd. Services page preview at :1898: OMT_COMMISSION_RATES['CASH_TO_BUSINESS'] is still 0.25 in the copied table -> 40 x 0.25 = $10.00 shown to the operator. $10.00 promised, $8.00 booked — structurally the same shape as the MTC/SMS case that prompted this audit.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: packages/core/src/utils/omtFees.ts. The frontend should import it. Verify first that omtFees is reachable from the renderer: the frontend resolves @liratek/core through packages/core/src/browser.ts, not index.ts, so the export must be present in BOTH entry points or the renderer dies at load (documented in memory as reference_core_browser_entrypoint).

divergences.title: A cashless settlement commission on a partner-uncovered fs row is stamped on the SUPPLIER_SETTLEMENT transaction but appears in neither the realized nor the deferred Profits bucket
divergences.detail: SupplierRepository.ts:1473-1474 stamps `profit_usd: batchModel === 1 ? data.commission_usd : 0` on the SUPPLIER_SETTLEMENT transaction for EVERY model-1 batch, cashless included. ProfitRepository.getSupplierCommissionTotals then never reads that stamp for a cashless batch (its billsOnly arm excludes it via `NOT cashlessCommissionBatch(source_id)`, :1512) and instead re-sources from settlement_commission_allocations weighted by `partnerCoverageRatio('financial_services','sca.financial_service_id')` (:1526-1527) — which is 0 for an uncovered partner row. getDeferredProfit does not catch the remainder either: its `partnerRow` (:1960-1968) weights by `1 - txnPartnerCoverageRatio(t)`, and that fragment correlates on `t.source_table`/`t.source_id`, which for a settlement row is `'supplier_ledger'` — no partner_ledger row ever carries that reference_table (stated at ProfitRepository.ts:945-950), so the ratio is 1.0 and the term is 0; its `cashlessDeferredRow` (:1993-2004) requires `NOT allocationNotDebtPending(sca)`, i.e. the CLIENT-debt axis only. So the partner axis has no deferred home for a cashless allocation.
divergences.workedExample: A FOR-partner OMT SEND, USD, amount $500, is settled today in a cashless batch; the operator enters commission_usd = $12.00 for it. Its partner_ledger FOR_% row is amount 500.00, covered_amount 0.00 (partner has paid nothing).  SUPPLIER_SETTLEMENT transaction stamp (SupplierRepository.ts:1473): profit_usd = $12.00.  getSupplierCommissionTotals.billsOnly (:1512): excluded, cashlessCommissionBatch is true.  getSupplierCommissionTotals.cashless (:1526): 12.00 x partnerCoverageRatio(0/500 = 0) = $0.00.  getDeferredProfit.partnerRow (:1961): 12.00 x (1 - 1.0) = $0.00 (settlement rows have no FOR_% partner_ledger row to correlate on).  getDeferredProfit.cashlessDeferredRow (:1993): debt is not pending, so `NOT allocationNotDebtPending` is false -> excluded -> $0.00.  Profits page: $0.00 realized, $0.00 deferred, for $12.00 that the settlement row itself stamps. Once the partner pays in full the ratio goes to 1 and the $12.00 appears — so it is deferred in effect, but the Deferred card reports 0 the whole time, which is what the Deferred card exists to prevent.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The exclusion from realized is right (owner decision, partner has not paid). The gap is the deferred bucket, which should surface the withheld share: the natural fix mirrors partnerRow's shape — `SUM(sca.commission_usd * (1 - partnerCoverageRatio('financial_services','sca.financial_service_id')))` over the same cashless allocation scan. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: this is derived by reading the four queries and composing them, not from a fixture run. Before filing, prove it with a test that creates a for-partner OMT SEND, settles it cashless, leaves partner_ledger.covered_amount at 0, and asserts both getSupplierCommissionTotals and getDeferredProfit return 0 — the failing-first shape rule 17 requires.

result.notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Read-only; no tests, builds or package commands were run, per the brief. Every cite below was opened and read; I did not trust any doc comment about code without reading the code it describes, and that caught two stale comments (listed under "stale comments" below). The five surfaces all exist for this module — none is absent.

WHAT AGREES, PLAINLY. Three things I checked and found clean, so they are not padding the list. (1) The OMT commission MATH is identical on both sides today: the frontend's copied OMT_COMMISSION_RATES and both fee tier tables (Services/index.tsx:66-124) match packages/core/src/utils/omtFees.ts value for value, including the LBP INTRA formula max(50,000, ceil(amount/1,000,000)*10,000). The duplication is a drift channel (divergence 11), not a live wrong number. (2) The USD transaction-day path agrees end to end: for a model-1 row the stamp writes 0 (FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1966-1979), ProfitRepository's transaction-day arm reads that same 0 stamp (:1565), and Closing's legacy arm is gated to model-0 only (:972/:985/:1000) — the LIRA-158 interlock holds in USD. The LBP hole (divergence 3) is a currency problem, not a model problem. (3) The Services page's StatsCards chips are currency-correct (StatsCards.tsx:37-45 consumes getAnalytics's byCurrency arrays) — it is the Profits Commissions tab that ignores the same payload.

THE ARCHETYPE DOES NOT REPEAT HERE IN ITS EXACT FORM. There is no OMT/Whish equivalent of "the preview subtracts one cost and the stamp subtracts two". The OMT preview is honest — it computes the same fee x rate the backend computes and labels it an estimate. The closest structural match is divergence 9 (app-wallet Shop Profit shown gross while the submitted commission subtracts the discount), which is the MTC shape with a discount instead of an SMS fee.

MOST LIKELY TO BE WORTH THE OWNER'S TIME, in order: divergence 2 ($90,002.00 versus $2.00 + 90,000 LBP is an absurd number an operator would notice and could not reconcile), divergence 3 (LBP commission is invisible in the daily closing document, which is the report the shop closes on), divergence 1 (the module's own page overstates unearned LBP profit by roughly 90,000x in apparent dollars), divergence 4 (fresh, introduced 2026-09-05, and the exact class LIRA-159's own body warns about).

SURFACES I DELIBERATELY WENT BEYOND THE FIVE FOR, and why. The Dashboard "Monthly Net Profit" tile (FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL:113-193) composes getRealizedCommissionTotals + getSupplierCommissionTotals, so it inherits divergence 6's definition rather than the Overview's stamp-based one — a sixth surface reporting a seventh number for the same money. I did not enumerate it as its own divergence because it is the same root cause as 6. The customer-session profit ledger is likewise outside the five but produced divergence 10.

TWO STALE COMMENTS FOUND WHILE VERIFYING (no numeric impact, but they will mislead the next reader). (a) FinancialRepository.ts:86-90 says it "Deliberately does NOT mirror ClosingRepository.getDailyStatsSnapshot's finProfitLegacy - that query is missing notPartnerPending/notDebtPending, a documented KNOWN GAP ... ticketed as LIRA-160." LIRA-160 shipped: both gates are present at ClosingRepository.ts:974, :986, :1000, :1003. (b) ClosingRepository.ts:49-51 says todayLocal "Mirrors the DATE(col,'localtime') = DATE('now','localtime') convention used across the reporting repositories (SalesRepository, FinancialServiceRepository)." SalesRepository does (:1627 et al.); FinancialServiceRepository.getAnalytics does not (:4728/:4746/:4760/:4778/:4793) — that is divergence 8.

ONE THING I COULD NOT SETTLE FROM CODE ALONE. Divergence 5 (Overview counts unsettled FS revenue, By-Date does not) is a recognition-basis question, not a bug with a right answer I can name. Both readings are defensible; what is indefensible is one page answering it twice. It needs the owner, in the same way LIRA-173 needed an interview.

WHAT I DID NOT COVER. I did not audit the REST twins in backend/src/api for envelope or gating parity on these queries, and I did not check the web-mode renderer — the brief scoped this to locating and comparing the five surfaces. I also did not verify divergence 12 against a fixture (its own caveat says so); it is the one entry on the list I would call Likely rather than Certain. Everything else on the list is re-derived from code I read at the cited lines.
