surfaces.location: packages/core/src/repositories/ProfitRepository.ts:1751-1776 (getMaintenanceTotals), :2405-2423 (getByDate's daily_maint CTE), :2750-2890 + :2910-3050 (getByUser / getByClient, generic ELSE branch); shared status fragment `maintenanceCompleted` at :970-972; assembled in packages/core/src/services/ProfitService.ts:403-404, :449-501, :601-614; rendered at frontend/src/features/profits/pages/Profits.tsx:1000-1035 (Overview card) and :1296-1360 (By Module table)
surfaces.formula: getMaintenanceTotals (:1754-1769): `SUM(m.final_amount_usd) AS revenue_usd, SUM(m.final_amount_lbp) AS revenue_lbp, SUM(m.cost_usd) AS cost_usd, SUM(m.cost_lbp) AS cost_lbp, SUM(t.profit_usd) AS profit_usd, SUM(t.profit_lbp) AS profit_lbp, COUNT(*) FROM maintenance m JOIN transactions t ON t.source_table='maintenance' AND t.source_id=m.id AND t.type='MAINTENANCE' WHERE m.status IN ('Delivered','Delivered_Paid') AND t.status='ACTIVE' AND COALESCE(m.is_refunded,0)=0 AND <notDebtPending(t.id)> AND datetime(m.created_at,'localtime') BETWEEN ? AND ?`. daily_maint (:2407-2422) is byte-equivalent plus `GROUP BY DATE(m.created_at,'localtime')`. getByUser/getByClient never name maintenance at all — it falls to the generic ELSE arms: revenue_usd `t.amount_usd * txnPartnerCoverageRatio(t)` (:2816), revenue_lbp bare `SUM(t.amount_lbp)` (:2817, no CASE, no gate), profit_usd/profit_lbp `t.profit_* * txnPartnerCoverageRatio(t)`; gated by `t.status='ACTIVE'`, `t.type IN (PROFIT_TXN_TYPES)` (:2883/:3038 — the list at :953-954 contains 'MAINTENANCE' and 'REFUND'), `datetime(t.created_at,'localtime') BETWEEN ? AND ?`, and a binary `WHEN NOT notDebtPending(t.id) THEN 0`. No partner gate anywhere on maintenance (correct — maintenance has no partner-routing path).
surfaces.currencies: revenue_usd/revenue_lbp/cost_usd/cost_lbp from `maintenance`; profit_usd/profit_lbp from `transactions`. Per-currency, no conversion.

surfaces.location: packages/core/src/repositories/ClosingRepository.ts:1216-1246 (the maintProfit arm), :1329-1335 (totalProfitUSD), :1360 (totalProfitLBP); rendered via frontend/src/features/closing/utils/rateStampedProfit.ts:126-207
surfaces.formula: `COALESCE(SUM(final_amount_usd - cost_usd), 0) as profit_usd FROM maintenance WHERE DATE(created_at,'localtime') = DATE('now','localtime') AND maintenance.status IN ('Delivered','Delivered_Paid') AND COALESCE(maintenance.is_refunded,0)=0 AND <notDebtPending(scalar txn subquery)> AND tenant_id = ?` (:1234-1245; the `!hasTransactionsTable` twin at :1223-1232 is the same expression minus the debt gate). It RECOMPUTES the margin off the source table instead of reading `transactions.profit_*` — the only one of the five surfaces that does. Feeds `totalProfitUSD` only (:1334). `totalProfitLBP` (:1360) is `lotoProfit.profit_lbp` and nothing else — there is no `maintProfit.profit_lbp`.
surfaces.currencies: totalProfitUSD only. No LBP field is ever populated from maintenance.

divergences.title: Every LBP maintenance job books 100% of its profit on the Profits page and exactly 0 in the daily closing
divergences.detail: The stamp is per-currency: MaintenanceService.ts:119-121 puts an LBP job's margin in `jobProfit`, and MaintenanceRepository.ts:379 writes it to `transactions.profit_lbp` (profit_usd stays 0). ProfitRepository.getMaintenanceTotals reads both columns (ProfitRepository.ts:1759-1760) so the LBP margin surfaces correctly. ClosingRepository.ts:1237 computes `SUM(final_amount_usd - cost_usd)` — USD columns only — and an LBP job has final_amount_usd = 0 and cost_usd = 0 by construction (frontend/src/features/maintenance/pages/Maintenance/index.tsx:186-196 `buildPricing` zeroes the unselected currency's columns). There is no LBP sibling query, and ClosingRepository.ts:1360 sets `totalProfitLBP = lotoProfit.profit_lbp` alone, so the LBP margin reaches NEITHER closing total. LBP is a first-class job currency here (create_db.sql:569-574 has cost_lbp/price_lbp/final_amount_lbp/currency; the page has a USD/LBP toggle at index.tsx:697-716). This CONFIRMS, for maintenance specifically, the item current_sprint.md's LIRA-176 lists as "Reported but NOT yet verified ... confirm module by module ... some may only ever have USD columns, which would be a non-issue" — for maintenance it is a real gap, not a non-issue.
divergences.workedExample: LBP job: cost 100,000 LBP, price 300,000 LBP, no discount, paid CASH in full today, status Delivered_Paid. Stored: currency='LBP', cost_lbp=100000, final_amount_lbp=300000, cost_usd=0, final_amount_usd=0. Stamp: profit_lbp = 300,000 - 100,000 = 200,000; profit_usd = 0. PROFITS (getMaintenanceTotals): revenue_lbp 300,000, cost_lbp 100,000, profit_lbp 200,000 -> the Maintenance card renders "Profit $0.00 + 200,000 LBP" (Profits.tsx:1029-1033). CLOSING (ClosingRepository.ts:1237): SUM(0 - 0) = 0 -> totalProfitUSD += $0.00; totalProfitLBP = 0. The Checkpoint PDF prints "Profit - USD amount: $0.00" and "Profit - LBP amount (Loto only): 0 LBP" (rateStampedProfit.ts:203-204). 200,000 LBP vs 0 LBP, same day, same job.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: profits. getMaintenanceTotals reads the stamp, which is the money of record; the closing arm should read `t.profit_usd`/`t.profit_lbp` off the joined transaction and contribute its LBP slice to `totalProfitLBP` (LIRA-176). rateStampedProfit.ts:36-45 already documents the mechanism and predicted exactly this.

divergences.title: Same job is dated by maintenance.created_at on three surfaces and transactions.created_at on two, and a multi-day repair reaches NO daily closing at all
divergences.detail: createJob writes `maintenance.created_at` when the device is RECEIVED (MaintenanceRepository.ts:195, :217). processPayments creates the transaction at CHECKOUT and passes no transaction_time, so `transactions.created_at` = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (MaintenanceRepository.ts:370-388 vs TransactionRepository.ts:507-508, which does accept one). Maintenance is the one module with a genuine multi-day draft lifecycle (Received -> In_Progress -> Ready -> Delivered_Paid; STATUS_TABS at index.tsx:43-70, the Start/Ready transition at index.tsx:236-267, "Save as Draft" at index.tsx:339-382), so the two timestamps routinely land on different days. getMaintenanceTotals (:1768) and daily_maint (:2407, :2420, :2422) date by `m.created_at`; getByUser (:2883-2884) and getByClient (:3038) date by `t.created_at`. The closing arm (ClosingRepository.ts:1238) uses `DATE(created_at,'localtime') = DATE('now','localtime')` on `maintenance` AND requires `status IN ('Delivered','Delivered_Paid')` in the same WHERE — a conjunction that can only be true when the job is received and delivered on the same calendar day.
divergences.workedExample: USD job. Device received Mon 2026-09-01 via "Save as Draft" (status Received, m.created_at = 09-01). Cost $20, price $50. Delivered and paid CASH Wed 2026-09-03 (t.created_at = 09-03, profit_usd stamp = $30). Query on Thu 09-04: Profits "By Module"/"By Date" for 09-01..09-01 -> Maintenance profit $30 (dated by m.created_at; status is now Delivered_Paid so maintenanceCompleted passes). Profits "By Cashier"/"By Client" for 09-01..09-01 -> $0; for 09-03..09-03 -> $30. Monday's closing snapshot: DATE(m.created_at)=today OK, but status on Monday was 'Received' -> maintenanceCompleted false -> $0. Wednesday's closing snapshot: status OK, but DATE(m.created_at)=09-01 != 09-03 -> $0. So $30 appears on 09-01 in one Profits tab, on 09-03 in another, and on NO day in any daily closing PDF.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Judgment call — this needs an owner decision (received-day vs delivered-day revenue recognition), not a code guess. But whichever day wins, all five surfaces must use ONE expression. Likely, based on every other module where source.created_at and txn.created_at coincide: `t.created_at` (the day money moved) is the intended basis, which would also make the closing arm reachable at all.

divergences.title: A fully-discounted job books negative profit in the closing and is invisible to Profits, because the closing reads the source table and Profits inner-joins the transaction
divergences.detail: MaintenanceService.saveJob only calls processPayments when `isPaidStatus && params.payments?.length` (MaintenanceService.ts:146, :186). A checkout whose net total is $0 completes with `payments: []` — CheckoutModal.handleComplete's only guards are the two debt guards (CheckoutModal.tsx:472-497), and `isPaymentComplete(0, 0)` is true (frontend/src/utils/paymentUtils.ts:115-118). The job is then saved with status 'Delivered_Paid' but NO transactions row. ClosingRepository.ts:1234-1245 queries `FROM maintenance` alone; its `notDebtPending(<scalar txn subquery>)` resolves to NULL, which the method's own doc (ClosingRepository.ts:340-358) states is trivially TRUE — so the row is counted and contributes `final_amount_usd - cost_usd`, i.e. minus the cost. ProfitRepository.getMaintenanceTotals (:1763) INNER JOINs transactions and drops the job entirely, from both profit and `count`.
divergences.workedExample: USD job: cost $20, price $50. Operator types 50 into the Discount field (CheckoutModal.tsx:893-899) -> finalAmount = max(0, 50-50) = $0 (CheckoutModal.tsx:355) -> completes with payments: []. Saved: status 'Delivered_Paid', final_amount_usd = 0, discount_usd = 50, cost_usd = 20, no transactions row. CLOSING: SUM(0 - 20) = -$20 subtracted from totalProfitUSD. PROFITS: JOIN transactions matches nothing -> $0 and count 0; the job does not appear on the By Module tab at all. -$20 vs $0 for the same job on the same day.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: profits. A job that produced no transaction moved no money and must contribute nothing; the closing arm should JOIN transactions (as getMaintenanceTotals does) rather than trusting `maintenance.status` alone. Whether a $0-net checkout should even be allowed to skip processPayments is a separate question worth raising.

divergences.title: By Module "Margin" reads 0% for an LBP job because the percentage divides the USD columns
divergences.detail: frontend/src/features/profits/pages/Profits.tsx:1352 renders the Margin cell as `formatPct(row.profit_usd, row.revenue_usd)`, and formatPct (Profits.tsx:290-293) returns the literal string "0%" when `total === 0`. An LBP maintenance row has profit_usd = 0 and revenue_usd = 0 by construction (the stamp is currency-exclusive, MaintenanceRepository.ts:378-379; the revenue columns are currency-exclusive, ProfitRepository.ts:1755-1756). The row's real LBP figures sit in the two adjacent LBP columns the Margin cell never reads. This is the identical shape to the MTC row that displayed 0% on 30,600/300,000.
divergences.workedExample: Same LBP job as divergence 1 (profit_lbp 200,000 on revenue_lbp 300,000 = 66.7%). The By Module row renders: Revenue (USD) $0.00 | Revenue (LBP) 300,000 LBP | Profit (USD) $0.00 | Profit (LBP) 200,000 LBP | Count 1 | Margin "0%". formatPct(0, 0) -> total === 0 -> "0%". The operator reads 0% next to a 200,000 LBP profit on the same row. Any month mixing USD and LBP maintenance jobs also understates the Margin, since only the USD slice reaches the ratio.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Neither column is wrong; the Margin cell is. It should compute per currency (two figures, matching the two revenue/profit column pairs), or render an em dash when revenue_usd is 0 and revenue_lbp is not — never a fabricated "0%". Same fix serves every LBP-capable module in that table, not just maintenance.

divergences.title: Maintenance checkout shows the "Keep change" button but the page never forwards kept_change_*, so the kept cash sits in the drawer with no profit row
divergences.detail: frontend/src/features/maintenance/pages/Maintenance/index.tsx:841 passes `allowKeepChange={true}`, which wires `onKeptChange` into MultiPaymentInput (CheckoutModal.tsx:990-992) and renders the button (MultiPaymentInput.tsx:1921-1938, label "Keeping ✓", panel heading "Change kept (profit)", title "Return nothing — keep the change as profit"). Turning it on sets `returnLegsValue = []` (MultiPaymentInput.tsx:1097), so `change_given_usd/lbp` come through as 0 and the drawer keeps the whole tender. CheckoutModal.getPaymentData emits `kept_change_usd`/`kept_change_lbp` (CheckoutModal.tsx:450-455), but the maintenance page's `handleCheckoutComplete` builds `jobData` field-by-field (index.tsx:394-416) and simply does not include them — it forwards change_given_* (:412-413) and stops. The whole backend chain accepts and stamps them: core validator (packages/core/src/validators/maintenance.ts:47-48), electron schema (electron-app/schemas/index.ts:325-328), service (MaintenanceService.ts:157-158), repository (MaintenanceRepository.ts:378-379). CheckoutModal's own prop doc (CheckoutModal.tsx:45-49) names Maintenance as the case where the fields "would be stripped ... and the change silently neither returned nor stamped"; MultiPaymentInput.tsx:1917-1920 calls it a "silent money hole". The e2e guard misses it because it hand-builds the IPC payload with `kept_change_usd: 3` and never drives the form (frontend/tests/e2e-electron/lira-108-keep-change-modules.spec.ts:95-135).
divergences.workedExample: USD job: cost $20, price $50, no discount. Customer hands $60 CASH; operator taps "Keep change". Modal payload: payments [{CASH, USD, 60}], change_given_usd 0, kept_change_usd 10. Page drops kept_change_usd -> service jobProfit = 50 - 20 = 30 -> MaintenanceRepository.ts:378 profit_usd = 30 + 0 = $30. Drawer: General/USD +$60, no change-out leg. Debt check (MaintenanceRepository.ts:503-509): 60 - 50 = -$10, no debt. Till now holds $60 against a $20 cost — a real $40 margin — while the stamp, the Profits card and the closing PDF all read $30. $10 disappears into the drawer with no profit row anywhere. The identical POS sale (frontend/src/features/sales/pages/POS/index.tsx:786) forwards the field and stamps $40.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: stamp (the core chain) is correct and complete. The bug is the page: add `...(paymentData.kept_change_usd || paymentData.kept_change_lbp ? { kept_change_usd, kept_change_lbp } : {})` to the jobData in index.tsx:394-416, following the pattern already used at frontend/src/features/loto/pages/Loto/index.tsx:301-307. Note this fix ALSO widens divergence 7 — see it.

divergences.title: Module history shows the pre-discount price while the ledger, Profits and closing all use the post-discount final amount
divergences.detail: The maintenance History modal's "Price" column and the jobs-list badge both render `price_lbp`/`price_usd` (HistoryModal.tsx:235-240; index.tsx:607-616) — the pre-discount list price. The transaction records `final_amount` (MaintenanceRepository.ts:375-376), and every accounting surface uses `final_amount_*` (ProfitRepository.ts:1755-1756, :2408-2409; ClosingRepository.ts:1237). The discount is reachable from the maintenance checkout (CheckoutModal.tsx:887-900). For an LBP job it is not even persisted anywhere: index.tsx:404-406 writes `discount_usd: cur === "USD" ? paymentData.discount || 0 : 0`, and there is no `discount_lbp` column (electron-app/create_db.sql:571) — so the difference is invisible on the row itself, with no field that explains it.
divergences.workedExample: LBP job: price 300,000 LBP, cost 100,000 LBP; operator applies a 50,000 LBP discount at checkout. Stored: price_lbp = 300,000, final_amount_lbp = 250,000, cost_lbp = 100,000, discount_usd = 0. History modal "Price" column -> "300,000 LBP". Jobs-list badge -> "300,000 LBP". transactions.amount_lbp -> 250,000. Profits revenue_lbp -> 250,000. The module's own history says the shop charged 300,000 LBP; the ledger and the Profits page say 250,000. 50,000 LBP of difference with no discount column on the row to account for it.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: stamp/profits (final_amount_*) — that is what was actually charged and collected. The History and jobs-list cells should render `final_amount_*` (falling back to `price_*` when it is 0, for pre-checkout drafts), or show both as "300,000 -> 250,000". A `discount_lbp` column would also close the LBP asymmetry.

divergences.title: Three independent hand-written definitions of "maintenance profit" with no shared fragment (rule 14)
divergences.detail: The margin is written out three times, in two languages: (1) TypeScript, both currencies, plus kept change — MaintenanceService.ts:119-121 with MaintenanceRepository.ts:378-379; (2) SQL, USD only, no kept change — ClosingRepository.ts:1226 and :1237; (3) SQL, both currencies, no kept change — the v101 backfill at packages/core/src/db/migrations/index.ts:4149-4162. Nothing links them. The contrast is instructive: the STATUS predicate for the same module IS shared — `maintenanceCompleted(alias)` (ProfitRepository.ts:970-972) is imported by ClosingRepository.ts:21 — and its own doc comment (ProfitRepository.ts:956-969) explains it was extracted precisely because a hand-copied second version drifted and left maintenance profit at a permanent $0 in every closing snapshot. The margin expression itself never got the same treatment.
divergences.workedExample: They are numerically equal today for a USD job ($50 - $20 = $30 in both), which is exactly why this reads as safe. Apply divergence 5's one-line frontend fix (forward kept_change_usd) and they part on the same transaction: customer hands $60 on a $50/$20 job with keep-change on. Definition (1) -> profit_usd = (50-20) + 10 = $40, so the Profits Maintenance card reads $40. Definition (2) -> SUM(final_amount_usd - cost_usd) = 50 - 20 = $30, so the same evening's closing PDF reads $30. A $10 discrepancy introduced by a fix that touches neither SQL query and would pass every existing test.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: stamp. `transactions.profit_usd`/`profit_lbp` is the money of record — every read surface should sum the stamp, and no query should re-derive the margin from `maintenance`. Concretely: give ClosingRepository the same `JOIN transactions ... t.type='MAINTENANCE'` shape getMaintenanceTotals uses. That single change closes divergences 1, 3 and 7 together.

divergences.title: Voiding a paid maintenance job drives By Cashier / By Client revenue negative while By Module and the closing correctly show zero
divergences.detail: MAINTENANCE is not in NON_REVERSIBLE_TRANSACTION_TYPES (packages/core/src/constants/transactionTypes.ts:219-232), so `transactions:void` (electron-app/handlers/transactionHandlers.ts:84-91) accepts it. The void path flips the original to VOIDED and inserts a reversal row carrying `original.type` — i.e. type 'MAINTENANCE', status ACTIVE, negated amounts — but OMITS profit_usd/profit_lbp from the INSERT column list entirely (TransactionRepository.ts:1371-1389), so they take the schema default 0 (electron-app/create_db.sql:112-113). getByUser/getByClient filter on `t.status='ACTIVE' AND t.type IN (PROFIT_TXN_TYPES)` (ProfitRepository.ts:2883, :3038) with no `notRefunded` on the source table, so the VOIDED original drops out and the ACTIVE negative reversal stays in. getMaintenanceTotals and the closing arm both gate on `notRefunded("m")` (ProfitRepository.ts:1766; ClosingRepository.ts:1240) and `_markSourceRefunded` has set `maintenance.is_refunded = 1`, so both correctly show zero. Not maintenance-specific — it applies to every module type in PROFIT_TXN_TYPES that is voided rather than refunded. The REFUND path is correct by contrast: TransactionRepository.ts:1614-1633 DOES carry `-original.profit_usd`/`-original.profit_lbp` and leaves the original ACTIVE, so a refund nets to zero on every surface.
divergences.workedExample: USD job: price $50, cost $20, paid CASH today, then voided the same day from the Transactions viewer. After the void: original row status VOIDED (profit $30); reversal row type 'MAINTENANCE', status ACTIVE, amount_usd -50, profit_usd 0; maintenance.is_refunded = 1. PROFITS By Module: notRefunded("m") false -> job excluded -> revenue $0.00, profit $0.00. CLOSING: same gate -> $0.00. PROFITS By Cashier: original excluded (VOIDED); reversal included -> revenue_usd += -50 x 1.0 = -$50, profit_usd += $0. That cashier's "Revenue (USD)" cell (Profits.tsx:1721) reads -$50.00 on a day where By Module shows $0.00 for Maintenance.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The refund path (TransactionRepository.ts:1614-1633) is the correct shape. The void reversal should either carry the negated profit stamp the same way, or the void reversal row should be recognisable and excluded — as written it removes revenue that the VOIDED original already stopped contributing, so it double-counts the reversal.

divergences.title: transaction_time is silently stripped on desktop but honoured on web, moving the same job to a different closing day per transport
divergences.detail: The maintenance page renders TransactionTimeOverride (index.tsx:18, :812-815) and sends `transaction_time` on both the draft path (:370) and the checkout path (:415). The desktop IPC handler validates against `MaintenanceJobSchema` in electron-app/schemas/index.ts:291-329 — a LOCAL duplicate of the core schema (its own comment at :323-325 admits the rule-14 debt) that has NO `transaction_time` key; the three other schemas in that file do (:513, :805, :900). `validatePayload` uses `safeParse` and returns `result.data` (electron-app/schemas/index.ts:1175-1182), and a plain `z.object` strips unknown keys, so the field never reaches MaintenanceService. The web REST route validates against the CORE schema instead (backend/src/api/maintenance.ts:6, :39), which DOES carry `transaction_time` (packages/core/src/validators/maintenance.ts:49). `note` and `paid_by` are stripped the same way; `issue_description` is REQUIRED on desktop (:293) but optional in core (validators/maintenance.ts:25). Separately, even on web only `maintenance.created_at` is backdated — processPayments never forwards transaction_time to createTransaction — which mechanically re-creates divergence 2 on every backdated web job.
divergences.workedExample: Operator sets Transaction Time to 2026-09-01 on a $50/$20 maintenance checkout entered on 2026-09-04. DESKTOP: field stripped -> maintenance.created_at = 2026-09-04 -> the $30 lands in the 09-04 closing snapshot and the 09-04 Profits bucket. WEB: field survives -> maintenance.created_at = 2026-09-01 -> the $30 lands in the 09-01 Profits bucket, and in NO closing snapshot at all (09-01's snapshot was taken before the job existed; 09-04's todayLocal test fails). Same operator action, same numbers, two different days depending on which build is running. On web, transactions.created_at still says 2026-09-04, so the By Cashier tab puts it on 09-04 either way.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The core schema (packages/core/src/validators/maintenance.ts) — CLAUDE.md rule 19b requires one schema lifted into packages/core and shared by both transports. Delete the electron-app duplicate and re-export `saveMaintenanceJobSchema` with the zod-major cast, as electron-app/schemas/index.ts already does for recharge (see its own note at :332-338). Then decide whether processPayments should forward transaction_time to createTransaction so both timestamps agree.

result.notes:
METHOD / LIMITS. Read-only, as instructed: I ran no tests, builds, yarn, npm or Playwright, and edited nothing. Every claim below is from source read this session; I re-opened each cited line rather than trusting a comment about it, since two of this repo's own comments turned out to disagree with the code (CheckoutModal.tsx:45-49 asserts Maintenance may not show the keep-change button, while index.tsx:841 sets allowKeepChange={true}; ClosingRepository.ts:1210-1216 states maintProfit needs only the notDebtPending axis, which is true for the gates but silently leaves the USD-only margin expression unexamined). Required reading done: CLAUDE.md (rules 13/14/18 in particular), docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md section 4, current_sprint.md at the repo root (NOT docs/tickets/CURRENT_SPRINT.md).

THE MTC ARCHETYPE DOES NOT EXIST HERE, AND CANNOT. The prompting bug was a live preview formula racing a stamp formula. Maintenance has no live profit preview at all (surface 1) and no profit/cost/margin column in its own history (surface 2) — verified by reading both files end to end, not by grep alone. The operator can enter a Repair Cost and a Price to Client and is never shown the difference, anywhere in the module. That absence is itself worth reporting: nothing in the maintenance UI would let an operator notice divergences 1, 3, 5 or 7. Whatever the closing PDF prints is the first and only number they see.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY CLEAN. The three surfaces that DO read the stamp agree exactly. getMaintenanceTotals (ProfitRepository.ts:1751-1776), getByDate's daily_maint (:2405-2423) and the ProfitService summary/module assembly (ProfitService.ts:449-501, :601-614) are per-currency throughout, apply the same five gates, and never convert LBP into USD. The v101 backfill (migrations/index.ts:4149-4162) is per-currency and correct for its era. maintenanceCompleted (ProfitRepository.ts:970-972) is genuinely shared between ProfitRepository and ClosingRepository (imported at ClosingRepository.ts:21) — that particular rule-14 debt was already paid, and its doc comment records why. Maintenance has no partner-routing path, and correctly carries no partnerCoverageRatio in any query. Refund symmetry is correct: the REFUND row carries the negated stamp (TransactionRepository.ts:1614-1633), `Maintenance Debt` is classified in notDebtPending's list (ProfitRepository.ts:406), and _cancelDebt covers it. The session-basket path is sound — SessionCheckoutService.ts:117 injects deferPayment: true, and processPayments returns before the drawer/change/debt block (MaintenanceRepository.ts:457-460) while still stamping full profit.

TWO THINGS I FOUND AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT FILE AS DIVERGENCES, so you know they were looked at:
1. getByUser/getByClient compute `revenue_lbp` as a bare `SUM(t.amount_lbp)` with no CASE and no debt gate (ProfitRepository.ts:2817, :2973) while every other column on those rows is gated — the method's own doc acknowledges it (ProfitRepository.ts:2716-2718). For an LBP maintenance job charged entirely to CUSTOMER_ACCOUNT the arithmetic diverges (By Cashier revenue_lbp 300,000 vs By Module revenue_lbp 0), but I could not make it user-visible: neither the By Cashier nor the By Client table declares a revenue_lbp column (Profits.tsx:1692-1700, :1760-1769), and DataTable's export is driven by the declared columns (packages/ui/src/components/ui/DataTable.tsx:567-569, :679-686), so it never reaches an operator's screen or export. Latent, not live.
2. The History modal's \"Price\" column declares `sortKey: \"price_usd\"` (HistoryModal.tsx:159) while the cell renders price_lbp for LBP rows — so sorting by Price files every LBP job under 0. Same class as LIRA-139's Amount-column fix. Cosmetic ordering, no number is wrong, so it is a follow-up rather than a divergence.

CROSS-REFERENCES TO THE LIVE BOARD. Divergence 1 is the maintenance answer to the module-by-module verification LIRA-176 explicitly asks for (current_sprint.md:3593-3615: \"Reported but NOT yet verified ... maintenance ... the mechanism may differ per module (some may only ever have USD columns, which would be a non-issue rather than a gap)\"). Divergences 3 and 7 are LIRA-160's unfinished half: that ticket added the gates to maintProfit but left the USD-only, source-recomputed margin expression untouched.

RANKING, if only one thing gets fixed: switch ClosingRepository's maintProfit to JOIN transactions and sum t.profit_usd/t.profit_lbp, contributing the LBP slice to totalProfitLBP. That one change closes divergences 1, 3 and 7 at once and removes the second hand-written copy of the margin. Divergence 5 (the dropped kept_change_*) is the only one where cash physically leaves the accounting model, so it is the highest per-incident cost even though it is rarer; note that fixing 5 before 7 actively widens 7.

SELF-ATTACK. The input that would flip the most here is my reading that `buildPricing` (index.tsx:186-206) really does zero the unselected currency's columns on every write path — if any path let cost_usd and cost_lbp be non-zero simultaneously, the stamp would drop one of them and divergence 1's arithmetic would change shape. Second: divergence 3's reachability rests on isPaymentComplete(0, 0) being true and on no other guard blocking a zero-payment checkout — I verified both (paymentUtils.ts:115-118; CheckoutModal.tsx:468-516) but did not execute it, so treat the reachability as Likely rather than Certain while the divergence between the two queries is Certain regardless of how the state is reached. Divergence 2's premise that repairs routinely span days is supported by the module's own design (four pre-delivery statuses, a draft button, a transition button) and by current_sprint.md:1316 describing exactly that lifecycle, but I have no production data on how often it actually happens.

divergences.workedExample: Buy back $10 of MTC credits for 800,000 LBP cash. Stamp: payoutUsd = 800,000/90,000 = 8.89; profit_usd = 10 - 8.89 = $1.11. Profits Overview / By-Module / By-Date: $0.00 (t.type is TELECOM_CREDIT_BUYBACK, not RECHARGE). Closing snapshot: 0 (currency LBP). By-User / By-Client: $1.11. Now the REST variant — POST /api/recharge/process with type CREDIT_BUYBACK, amount 10, price 900 and no `currency` key: the row is written currency_code 'USD', price 900, cost 0. Closing snapshot adds price - cost = +$900 to totalProfitUSD for a transaction where $900 of cash LEFT the drawer; the stamp for the same row says profit_usd = 10 - 900 = -$890. A $1,790 swing on one row.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp (credits gained minus cash paid is the real spread). Both reporting surfaces are wrong in opposite directions: the Profits arms omit the type entirely, and the closing arm needs a recharge_type/transaction-type filter so it can never read a payout as revenue.

divergences.title: The MTC/Alfa tab header 'Profit' metric reads `financial_services`, a table that holds no telecom rows — it is permanently $0.00
divergences.detail: Recharge/index.tsx:1381-1383 feeds CompactStats from `telecomStats` (index.tsx:1328-1358), which filters `finTransactions`. `finTransactions` is loaded at index.tsx:359-366 from `api.getOMTHistory(activeProvider)` -> backendApi.ts:1401-1411 -> omtHandlers.ts:72 `financialService.getHistory(provider)` -> the `financial_services` table. Telecom recharges are written only to `recharges` (the six INSERT sites are all in RechargeRepository.ts: :478, :646, :1318, :1510, :1623, :1755, and none of them is a financial_services insert). So for provider 'MTC' or 'Alfa' the filter at index.tsx:1329-1331 always yields an empty array and CompactStats.tsx:110-113 falls through to `$0.00`. Verified against the live DB: financial_services holds exactly one row, provider WHISH_APP; recharges holds the two MTC/Alfa rows.
divergences.workedExample: On 2026-09-06 the shop booked 30,600 LBP (MTC) and 61,200 LBP (Alfa) of stamped profit. Open the Recharge page on the MTC tab as an admin: the header reads 'Profit $0.00' and 'Count 0'. Open the MTC History modal on the same screen: it lists the row with 45,000 LBP. The Profits page says 30,600 LBP. Three figures on two screens for one sale — $0.00, 45,000, 30,600.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp. The header metric is reading the wrong table entirely for these two providers; it should aggregate `rechargeHistory` (already loaded at index.tsx:697-729) or, better, the stamped profit.

divergences.title: maxDiscount is derived from the SMS-free gross margin, so the sheet offers a discount that would take the stamped profit negative
divergences.detail: TelecomForm.tsx:897-906 sets the PaymentSheet's `maxDiscount` to `price - amount * alfaCreditCostRate` — the fourth hand-written copy of the gross-margin expression in this feature (the others: TelecomForm.tsx:815-822, CardGridPayView.tsx:128, CardGridPayView.tsx:250-253), none of which subtracts the SMS fee the stamp subtracts. Compounding it: `onDiscountChange` is never passed to TelecomForm from Recharge/index.tsx (grep of index.tsx finds no such prop), so the discount reduces the payment legs but never reduces the submitted `data.price`. RechargeRepository.ts:853-866 then runs reconcileLegs against the un-discounted price; with a client selected `autoDebtRemainder` (TelecomForm.tsx:1160-1162) is true, so the discount silently lands as client debt instead.
divergences.workedExample: MTC $3 at 300,000 LBP. The sheet advertises a maximum discount of 45,000 LBP. Take it: the customer pays 255,000. The submitted price is still 300,000, so the stamp books profit_lbp = 300,000 - 255,000 - 14,400 = 30,600 while only 255,000 of cash arrived — and the 45,000 shortfall is booked as a 'Recharge Debt' charge on the client, or hard-rejected by reconcileLegs if no client is selected. Had the discount reached `price`, the stamped profit would have been 255,000 - 255,000 - 14,400 = -14,400 LBP, against a preview that presented 45,000 as the safe floor.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The stamp. maxDiscount must be the NET margin (gross minus the SMS fee), and the discount must reach the submitted price — otherwise the ceiling is both too high and disconnected from what is actually booked.

divergences.title: The Alfa Gift card grid prices from a localStorage key nothing ever writes, so it ignores the configured sell rate the Credit tab obeys
divergences.detail: TelecomForm.tsx:339-348 builds each gift tier's `sellLbp` from `Number(localStorage.getItem('alfa_credit_sell_rate_lbp') || '100000') / 1000`, then multiplies back by 1000 at :347. A repo-wide grep for that key finds only four sites: this localStorage read, Recharge/index.tsx:297-299 (system_settings), and ShopConfig.tsx:122/:214 (reads and WRITES system_settings via api.updateSetting). Nothing ever writes it to localStorage, so the getItem always returns null and the grid is permanently pinned to 100,000. The Credit tab's suggested price (Recharge/index.tsx:1301, :1320) uses the configured value. The grid's cost side, by contrast, DOES honour settings (TelecomForm.tsx:252-267 reads `alfa_credit_cost_lbp`), so the two halves of the card's own displayed Profit (CardGridPayView.tsx:128) are sourced from different places. The live DB confirms the state: neither `alfa_credit_sell_rate_lbp` nor `alfa_credit_cost_lbp` is present in system_settings, so both currently sit on their defaults.
divergences.workedExample: Admin sets Shop Config sell rate to 110,000 LBP/$ (written to system_settings). Credit tab, $3.50: suggested price 3.50 x 110,000 = 385,000 LBP. Alfa Gift '1 GB' tier (ALFA_GIFT_TIERS at frontend/src/features/recharge/types/index.ts:208, usd 3.5): sellLbp = round(3.5 x (100000/1000) x 1000) = 350,000 LBP. costLbp = 3.5 x 85,000 = 297,500 either way. Displayed card profit 52,500 LBP; the profit the same $3.50 would make on the Credit tab at the configured rate is 87,500 LBP. A 35,000 LBP gap per card, and the gift price the operator charges is 35,000 below the rate the owner set.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: Recharge/index.tsx's system_settings read. localStorage is not a configuration store here — nothing writes it, and ShopConfig is the only place the owner can set the rate.

divergences.title: On the Days tab, `default_price_to_client` is a day count multiplied by a per-dollar sell rate, which disables the history's margin-override alert
divergences.detail: Recharge/index.tsx:507 sets `amount = parseFloat(telecomAmount)`, which for rechargeType DAYS is a DAY COUNT (confirmed by RechargeRepository.ts:308-314 and :355-363, telecomStockLeg's DAYS arm). Line :516 then computes `defaultPriceToClient = amount * alfaCreditSellRate` unconditionally and ships it at :594. HistoryModal.tsx:307-315 compares the row's actual price against that value to raise the red 'Margin' theft-detection badge. For DAYS the reference is in the wrong unit by roughly two orders of magnitude, so `marginOverride` is always deeply negative and the badge at HistoryModal.tsx:341-349 can never fire.
divergences.workedExample: Sell 30 days for 200,000 LBP (cost side: costOfValidityDaysUsd(30) = 0.90 USD -> 76,500 LBP; preview profit 123,500 LBP). default_price_to_client is stored as 30 x 100,000 = 3,000,000 LBP. History modal: actualPrice = cost + commission = 76,500 + 123,500 = 200,000; marginOverride = 200,000 - 3,000,000 = -2,800,000; the threshold test `marginOverride > 100,000` fails. Now let an operator overcharge that same 30-day sale at 900,000 LBP: marginOverride = -2,100,000, still no alert — the badge is structurally dead on the Days tab, whereas on the Credit tab a 900,000-vs-300,000 overcharge would raise it.
divergences.suspectedAuthority: The Credit tab's semantics. `default_price_to_client` is defined as 'credits x sell-rate-per-dollar'; the Days tab has no equivalent reference price, so it should send null (the column is nullable — RechargeRepository.ts:657 already writes `?? null` and HistoryModal.tsx:309 already handles null) rather than a wrong-unit number.

result.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — I could not refute it on reachability. Every link in the chain is live, operator-reachable, and rendered.

AUTHORITY SIDE (stamp), all cites exact:
- `SalesRepository.ts:530` `saleProfitUsd -= sale.discount || 0`; rationale comment at :492-495 ("the discount comes straight out of the shop's margin (final_amount = total − discount), so gross item margins alone overstate profit on every discounted sale").
- Refund arm re-derives it pro-rata: `SalesRepository.ts:1439-1442` (`lineShareOfSale` :1439-1440, `discountShareUsd` :1441, `refundProfitUsd = grossMarginUsd - discountShareUsd` :1442). Claim said :1436-1442 — that range includes the leading comment; the executable lines are 1439-1442.
- `SalesRepository.discountProfit.test.ts:4-7` states the pre-fix behavior in the claim's exact words ("Every discounted sale overstated profit by the full discount") and asserts stamp = margins − discount (:196 `toBe(70)`, :253/:263 net-to-zero on refund). So the stamp is a deliberate, guarded fix, not an accident.
- Profits page realized sales profit reads that stamp: `ProfitRepository.ts:1303` `SUM(t.profit_usd * saleRecognitionWeight("s"))`.

DIVERGENT SIDE — all four cites land exactly on the claimed expression, and none carries a discount term:
- `ClosingRepository.ts:871` (inside `getDailyStatsSnapshot()`, :814) — verified `grep -n discount ClosingRepository.ts` returns ZERO hits in the whole file.
- `FinancialRepository.ts:130` (`getMonthlyPL`, :114) — ZERO `discount` hits in the file.
- `SalesRepository.ts:1999` (profit branch of the chart query).
- `ProfitRepository.ts:3066` `SELECT SUM((si.sold_price_usd - si.cost_price_snapshot_usd) * si.quantity)` → `AS potential_profit_usd` :3069 — ZERO `s.discount`/`discount_usd` hits in the file.

REACHABILITY (my assigned lens — I tried to kill it here and could not):
1. Discount input is ungated and always rendered: `CheckoutModal.tsx:895` `data-testid="checkout-discount-input"` inside the always-on Order Summary block (:882-900). No permission check, no feature flag.
2. It reaches the payload: `CheckoutModal.tsx:428` `discount: discount` → written to `discount_usd` at `SalesRepository.ts:473`.
3. The line items are NOT discount-allocated — this was the one input that could have flipped the verdict. `SalesRepository.ts:764-767` inserts `sold_price_usd` from `itemStmt.run(..., item.price, ...)` (:901-911), and POS sends `price: item.retail_price` (`POS/index.tsx` cart map). So `sold_price_usd` is the PRE-discount unit price; the stamp is not double-subtracting.
4. No compensating write anywhere: SalesRepository's only side-ledger insert is the sale debt (`:1576 INSERT INTO debt_ledger`) — no expense row, no negative-profit row, no discount line in the closing report.
5. All four surfaces render for the SAME transaction type (SALE):
   - Closing PDF: `Checkpoint/index.tsx:301` `api.getDailyStatsSnapshot()` → `generateClosingReport(..., dailyStats, sellRate)` (:313); `salesProfit.profit_usd` is summed into `totalProfitUSD` at `ClosingRepository.ts:1330`.
   - Dashboard tile: `Dashboard.tsx:388` `api.getMonthlyPL(localMonth())` → :396 `monthlyNetProfitUSD`.
   - Dashboard chart: `Dashboard.tsx:383` `api.getProfitSalesChart(chartType)`; "Profit" is one dropdown selection away (:1285-1290).
   - Profits pending tab: `Profits.tsx:487` `api.getPendingProfit`, tab registered :542, `potential_profit_usd` typed :381.
6. Gates do not separate them: Closing requires `saleFullyPaid("s")` (:876) and the stamp has no such gate, so a fully-paid discounted sale shows $20 on Profits and contributes $40 to the closing total the same day. `getMonthlyPL` has no fully-paid gate at all — `FinancialRepository.ts:110-113` explicitly names the ONE predicate it deliberately omits (fully-paid) and says nothing about a deliberate discount omission, which is affirmative evidence the discount was missed rather than intended.

Self-attack: the strongest counter is "Closing is a deliberate gross-of-discount cash view." Nothing supports that — no comment in either file mentions discount at all, while the writing side documents the opposite rule and guards it with two tests.
result.correction:
The finding stands; three details need tightening before it is filed.

1. Line cite: the refund arm's executable lines are `SalesRepository.ts:1439-1442`, not :1436-1442 (:1436-1438 are comment). All four divergent cites (ClosingRepository.ts:871, FinancialRepository.ts:130, SalesRepository.ts:1999, ProfitRepository.ts:3066) are byte-exact — do not "correct" those.

2. Magnitude on two of the four surfaces is stated too strongly. The Dashboard tile does not display "$40.00": `Dashboard.tsx:396` renders `monthlyNetProfitUSD`, a NET figure (sales arm + commissions − expenses). The correct statement is that its sales arm contributes $40 instead of $20, so the tile over-reports net profit by exactly the discount, $20. Same for the closing document: the figure printed is the cross-module aggregate `totalProfitUSD` (`ClosingRepository.ts:1330`), so the PDF's total profit is over by $20 — it does not show a standalone $40. The Dashboard chart also requires the operator to switch the trend selector from its default "Sales" to "Profit" (`Dashboard.tsx:290` default, :1285-1290 selector) — still reachable in one click, but it is not the default view.

3. Interaction with the quantity bug, which the claim under-specifies. `ProfitRepository.ts:3066` DOES multiply by `si.quantity`, so on the Profits pending tab the missing discount is the ONLY defect and the over-promise equals the full discount at ANY quantity. The other three (ClosingRepository.ts:871, FinancialRepository.ts:130, SalesRepository.ts:1999) omit `* si.quantity` as well, and that error runs the OPPOSITE direction, so at qty > 1 their net error is not "exactly the discount" — the two defects partially offset and the sign depends on the cart. The claim's qty-1 worked example is therefore correct as written and is the right example to file, but the ticket must not generalize "over-reports by exactly the discount" to those three surfaces at qty > 1; fix the discount term and the quantity term together, or the closing number will move in a direction the owner cannot predict from either ticket alone.

result.correction:
Three corrections; the finding itself stands.

1. WRONG LINE. The em-dash render is frontend/src/features/profits/pages/Profits.tsx:1348-1350, not 1350-1352.

2. THE USD HALF IS OVERSTATED. `kept_change_usd` reaches EVERY Profits tab, because all of them source sale profit from the stamp, not from sale_items: Overview via ProfitRepository.getSalesProfit (:1300-1319, `SUM(t.profit_usd * saleRecognitionWeight(s))`), By-Module via the same call (ProfitService.ts:538/547), By-Date via the `daily_sales_profit` CTE (:2321-2340, summed at :2481), By-User (:2832), By-Client (:2985). Only sale_items is used for revenue/cost, where kept change correctly does not belong. The USD blind spots are exactly TWO queries, both of which recompute sale profit from sale_items instead of reading the stamp: ClosingRepository.ts:868-879 and FinancialRepository.ts:126-140. Worth flagging while there: both compute `SUM(sold_price − cost_price_snapshot)` and so also miss the sale-level `discount` that SalesRepository.ts:530 subtracts from the stamp — a larger, separate divergence than kept change, and FinancialRepository.ts:126-140 omits `* si.quantity` as well.
